iOS 27.2 launched last week with a convenient new Messages feature called ‘Suggested Actions.’ Here’s how you can customize the feature to your liking.
If your iPhone is running iOS 27.2, you might have noticed a handy addition in the Messages app.
Whenever a message contains actionable information—an event you might want to add to your calendar, or todo you need reminding of—Messages will add a ‘Suggested Action’ right below the relevant message.
Using these new suggestions, with a quick tap you can turn the message into an action. And they’re so small and unobtrusive in the UI that they don’t clutter up the app at all.
But depending on your needs, you might want to enable or disable some of these suggestions. And Apple lets you do that with a surprising level of granularity.
Inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Messages -> Suggested Actions you’ll find customization options for the feature.
There are five different types of suggestions that can be enabled or disabled in Settings. By default, all five are enabled.
Here are the five categories:
I’m planning to leave all five enabled, because I’ve found the feature a useful addition. But it’s great to see Apple offer a refreshing level of control like this right off the bat.
Note: Suggested Actions are powered by Apple Intelligence, so you’ll need an AI-compatible iPhone to get the feature.

articles.title_zh: Googling "Zelda" today offers a glimpse of how search worked in 1998
articles.content_orig:
The year was 1998. Britney Spears topped the charts, Bill Clinton was impeached, and a couple of little websites called Google and Ars Technica came online. It was also the year Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. Google, which has come to dominate the Internet (Ars is still working on that), is celebrating the imminent release of the Ocarina of Time remaster by temporarily transporting us back to that storied year with a search Easter egg.
To access the Google time machine, you just have to search for either “Zelda” or “Ocarina of Time.” Google will load the standard 2026 results page, but you’ll see an animated Master Sword in the lower right corner. It appears on both mobile and desktop—just click the sword and enjoy the show.
After a little time-skipping animation and a Link shout (you know the one), you’ll swear it’s 1998 again. The search page is transformed into a simple list of blue links with retro Google branding. This is particularly apt given the time-shifting mechanics in Ocarina of Time .
Classic Google used to provide a list of 10 links on each page, but there are only seven included in the Easter egg. This is a curated list of links rather than a real search. You get the official Nintendo Zelda page, Zelda on Wikipedia, Zelda games on Amazon, and a couple more.
You can go back to the modern version of Google’s search results at any time by clicking the sword again. Oh, you don’t want to do that? Sadly, this is a very limited experience. The Google of today is much different, and if you try to search for anything from the retro interface, you are immediately booted back to 2026 with all the AI, sponsored content, suggested searches, and social media links.
The Ocarina of Time left its mark on a generation of gamers, and clearly, some of them went on to work at Google. The company’s intention is probably to leverage nostalgia to build hype for Nintendo’s big launch, but there’s also something a little sad about this. Google’s push into generative AI is transforming search in a way that many people don’t like. Seeing the simple, minimalist roots of Google search on display drives home how much the company’s core product has changed.
The Ocarina of Time has changed a lot, too. The remastered game has been completely re-created, with slick Switch 2 graphics, modern controls for movement and camera, numerous quality-of-life improvements, and more. The game is available for preorder now at $60 for digital and $70 for physical. It launches on November 5 for Nintendo Switch 2.

articles.title_orig: China Lays Out Four Missions Leading to a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.title_zh: China Lays Out Four Missions Leading to a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.content_orig:
China has published a mission-by-mission schedule for landing astronauts on the Moon before 2030, about a year behind NASA's 2028 target, Ars Technica reported. It is the most detailed public account so far of the country's lunar program.
Wang Xiang presented the plan on October 31 at the 7th Manned Space Academic Conference. He is deputy chief designer of China's Manned Space Program and chief designer of its lunar exploration project.
The two-day event at Beihang University was hosted by the China Manned Space Agency. It drew more than 800 experts and scholars, BigGo Finance reported.
Slides from the presentation list these steps, according to Ars Technica:
BigGo Finance summarised the 2028 to 2030 window differently. It said Wenchang, the launch site in Hainan, will host three uncrewed lunar orbit verification missions and one crewed landing.
Three astronauts would make the trip, with two going down to the surface, Shattered reported, citing Chinese state media. The third would stay in orbit aboard Mengzhou.
China lacks a rocket as powerful as the Saturn V. So the crew ship and lander launch separately. Shattered said this lets controllers confirm the lander reached lunar orbit before the crew commits to the trip.
After docking in lunar orbit, the two astronauts move into the lander and descend. They lift off, dock with Mengzhou a second time and return to Earth in the spacecraft, BigGo Finance said.
Development is under way on the lander, a moonwalk spacesuit and a crewed lunar rover.
There is no Apollo 8 or Artemis II equivalent in this plan. In those missions, a crew flies to the Moon and returns without landing, Ars Technica noted. Mengzhou will still carry astronauts to the Tiangong space station in low-Earth orbit.
In August 2025, the China Manned Space Agency tested a high-fidelity mock-up of the 26-ton Lanyue lander near Beijing. Tethers simulated lunar gravity. On February 11, Mengzhou passed a maximum dynamic pressure abort test and splashed down safely at sea.
BigGo Finance described it as China's first at-sea recovery of a crewed spacecraft.
Mengzhou has also arrived at Wenchang for the 2027 test flight. On October 22, the agency asked Chinese institutions to propose payloads for the uncrewed Lanyue flight. Shattered reported a March 1, 2027 deadline for those proposals.
It also said no firm date has been given for the crewed mission.
Ars Technica said NASA's schedule depends on lunar landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin. A US landing could slip to 2030 or later. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has cancelled the Lunar Gateway space station.
He has also cancelled planned upgrades to the Space Launch System rocket.
Shattered reported that Artemis III is now a crewed Earth-orbit test in 2027. The first landing moves to Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028.
I cover what the internet is actually talking about: the new release, the viral moment, the creator beef, the product launch. My job is to explain it fast and clearly, without the breathless hype. I read the timeline…

articles.title_orig: Poland's constitutional crisis deepens as Prime Minister Tusk faces accusations of power grab
articles.title_zh: Poland's constitutional crisis deepens as Prime Minister Tusk faces accusations of power grab
articles.content_orig:
Protesters gathered outside Poland’s top court as a long-running political dispute involving President Karol Nawrocki and Donald Tusk’s government escalated.  (AP Video.)
Friday’s late-night confrontation at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which drew riot police and protesters and prompted President Karol Nawrocki to turn his plane around and return to Warsaw, has reignited a bitter debate over whether Prime Minister Donald Tusk is restoring the rule of law or overstepping constitutional limits.
The dispute erupted after the tribunal announced the suspension of its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, a move that supporters of Tusk’s government described as necessary to restore judicial independence, while critics denounced it as an unconstitutional power grab.
Marcin Przydacz, the head of the International Policy Bureau in Nawrocki’s office, took to European TV Monday morning denouncing Tusk’s actions, saying, "Even lawyers who are close to the Tusk government say that there's absolutely no legal basis for such behavior."
POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT
Donald Tusk, Poland's prime minister, during the Polish Army Parade in Warsaw on Aug. 15, 2025. (Damian Lemanski/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The dispute is also triggering diplomatic fallout, with at least three Polish ambassadors resigning in protest. Przydacz, a former parliament member of the now-opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, says Poland’s permanent representative to the U.N. since 2021, Krzysztof Szczerski, resigned Monday, which followed the resignations over the weekend of the ambassadors to China and Romania.
"This crisis didn’t begin on Friday," said Simone Rodan‑Benzaquen, senior envoy to Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. "Poland has been living with a deeply compromised Constitutional Tribunal for more than a decade."
Rodan-Benzaquen said the confrontation cannot be understood in isolation. Parliament has continued appointing judges under Poland's constitution, but several of those appointments have been blocked from taking office amid a years-long standoff between the government, the presidency and the tribunal itself.
Presidential candidate Karol Nawrocki, a conservative historian backed by the right-wing Law and Justice party, second right, greets supporters at his headquarters after the presidential election runoff in Warsaw, Poland, June 1, 2025. (AP Photo/Czarek Sokolowski)
"This isn't simply a case of Tusk deciding to pack a functioning, independent court ahead of an election," Rodan-Benzaquen tells Fox News Digital. "There is a genuine institutional crisis that predates his government, and a legitimate question of how to resolve it."
That underlying conflict exploded into public view Friday after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended Święczkowski and his deputy, triggering protests outside the tribunal and prompting Nawrocki to abandon a trip to Senegal. Police detained three people after some demonstrators clashed with officers outside the court complex.
HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNREST
Rodan-Benzaquen cautioned that concerns about Friday's actions are not limited to supporters of the opposition, saying they "raise serious questions about the legality and proportionality of the methods being used."
Critics of the government have described Friday's events as an unprecedented assault on Poland's constitutional order. "My former boss, Margaret Thatcher, would have been absolutely appalled by what we're witnessing in Poland," Nile Gardner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation told Fox News Digital. "This is clearly a crisis for Poland and an attempted coup by Donald Tusk."
"This has all the hallmarks of a Soviet-style coup operation," added Gardner, who said Tusk waited until Nawrocki was traveling out of the country, accusing the prime minister of undermining the tribunal and further destabilizing Poland ahead of next year's election. "It's the sort of thing you'd expect actually from a third world dictator."
Protesters gather outside the headquarters of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after police blocked access to the court building on Oct. 30, 2026 (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP via Getty Images)
Others reject the coup characterization. Boštjan Udovič, chair of international relations at the University of Ljubljana, says the dispute centers on the government's attempt to restore judicial arrangements that critics of the previous PiS government say were inconsistent with both Poland's constitution and European legal standards.
"Tusk wants to restore the situation as required by the constitution and the international institutions," Udovič said. "I think that he hoped the transition would be easier."
Tusk defended his government's actions as part of an effort to restore the rule of law, accusing both the president and the tribunal of improperly blocking judges elected by parliament from taking office. "The solution to the conflict is simple," he said on Monday. "The president recognizes the judges legally elected by [parliament], because that is what the Constitution stipulates." He accused Nawrocki of "choosing forceful confrontation, which could cost Poland very dearly. A democratic state under the rule of law cannot yield to violence."
POLAND ARRESTS RUSSIAN ALLEGEDLY HIRED TO KILL UKRAINIAN-AMERICAN WHO WAS 'INCONVENIENT TO THE PUTIN REGIME'
"Restoring the rule of law is essential," Rodan-Benzaquen says, warning against viewing the dispute purely through a partisan lens. "But the legitimacy of that restoration depends not only on its objectives, but also on the legality of the means used to achieve it."
The divide in Poland has increasingly been reflected abroad, with European institutions and political leaders offering sharply different interpretations of the crisis.
Protesters rally outside Poland’s top court as tensions between President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government intensify. (AP)
The European Commission has largely backed the Polish parliament's authority to appoint judges. European Commissioner Michael McGrath said selecting new judges lies within the powers of Poland's parliament.
French opposition leader Marine Le Pen , meanwhile, accused Brussels of applying a double standard. "One cannot claim to defend democracy and the rule of law while remaining silent when the constitutional balance of a member state is gravely threatened," she posted on X. "The proliferation of such strong-arm tactics within the European Union itself is beginning to raise serious questions."
"America is on Poland’s side," U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose posted to X , urging restraint. "Our concern is for the stability, security, and democratic future of a country we are proud to call our friend and ally… Poland has come too far and accomplished too much to let political differences, no matter how strongly felt, put any of that at risk."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Police were deployed outside the Constitutional Tribunal after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, elected by the Parlament in March 2026, issued an order suspending Tribunal President Bogdan Swieczkowski and Vice President Bartlomiej Sochanski from their duties for one month. (Kai Taller/Arena Akcji/Sipa USA)
For Rodan-Benzaquen, the larger issue extends far beyond the events of Friday night. "One side claims to be defending constitutional order against the abuses of the other, while the institutions that should arbitrate the dispute have themselves become the object of the dispute," she said.
With parliamentary elections in Poland only a year away, the battle over who gets to define the rule of law may prove more consequential than the confrontation that unfolded this weekend.

articles.title_orig: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
articles.title_zh: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027.
The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements.
He added that the Trump administration had additionally notified the two countries of the decision.
The Trump administration cited barriers to US trade and investment, as well as concerns over national security and foreign policy interests in the region.
In Rwanda's case, Washington also raised concerns about human rights, political pluralism, the rule of law and workers' rights.
The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by US Treasury for its alleged role in the armed rebellion in eastern DR Congo.
The US Treasury said Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training.
For South Africa, the US additionally pointed to corruption.
"The Trump administration is working to ensure our African partners take the necessary steps to meet the eligibility criteria," Greer said.
The announcement comes amid strained relations between Washington and both countries, with the proposed termination threatening their access to preferential trade arrangements with the US.
Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House and launched a US refugee pathway for Afrikaners.
US Ambassador to South Africa Leo Brent Bozell III said it was regrettable that South African policies led to its termination from Agoa.
"This was a predictable and preventable outcome resulting from the rejection by South Africa's government of real concerns raised by the US," he wrote on X.

articles.title_orig: Weil Associate Blasts ‘Greed’ And ‘Lack Of Leadership’ As Firm Collapses
articles.title_zh: Weil Associate Blasts ‘Greed’ And ‘Lack Of Leadership’ As Firm Collapses
articles.content_orig:
Ed. note : Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day .
Everyone has to look out for number one at this point. Everyone has to find new jobs.
I understand that [Biglaw] is a very cut-throat environment, but just the level of greed combined with the lack of leadership from the top of the firm was truly disappointing. You had people on the management committee who signed up to lead the firm through whatever came, and instead of shepherding the firm through a very difficult time, they used their insider information to negotiate deals with other firms and oftentimes leaving associates behind.
— An anonymous Weil Gotshal associate, speaking to Bloomberg Law as the nearly century-old firm prepares to wind down and send nearly 600 associates into the job market. The associate said they received more than 100 LinkedIn requests from headhunters in the two days after Executive Partner Barry Wolf announced the news. Recruiter Blair Broser said associates “don’t have any leverage at this time,” while recruiter Summer Eberhard said Weil lawyers remain marketable for their credentials and sophisticated experience. Associates and staff have been told they’ll receive salary and benefits for 90 days, with bonuses available to those who stay until near year-end.
Staci Zaretsky is the managing editor of Above the Law, where she’s worked since 2011. She’d love to hear from you, so please feel free to email her with any tips, questions, comments, or critiques. You can follow her on Bluesky , X/Twitter , and Threads , or connect with her on LinkedIn .

articles.title_zh: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
articles.content_orig:

Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.
Squarespace, the web company that helps customers build and host their own websites, is laying off about one-fifth of its workforce, in a move that will affect hundreds of jobs.
Jeff Seedman, a public relations specialist representing Squarespace, confirmed the layoffs to TechCrunch. The Verge initially reported the layoffs.
“Squarespace is restructuring its organization and reducing its global workforce by approximately 19%, representing around 300 employees,” said Seedman. “The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth.”
Website building has changed immensely over the last few years as a result of the generative AI boom. “Vibe-coding” website builders, which only require simple prompts from users to spin up functional front-end designs, have largely upended the industry, making it possible for users to create sites with significantly less effort.
These kinds of sites have become an increasingly central part of the website-building business. Last year, web host rival Wix bought Base44 for $80 million . Similar offerings, like Lovable, have generated significant investor interest; Lovable raised a $400 million Series C round in August that valued the company at $13.3 billion. Google also recently launched Stitch , a feature that allows users to swiftly generate user-interface designs.
Squarespace has also begun a big push into AI. In 2024, the company launched an AI tool called Blueprint. The company also recently announced Forma, an upcoming AI native platform, whose waitlist users can join .
Squarespace was founded in 2004 and went public in 2021 at a $10 billion valuation. However, the company struggled in the ensuing years to generate enthusiastic public market interest. Squarespace ultimately decided to go private again by way of a $7 billion private equity deal in 2024.
An earlier version of this report incorrectly stated that Squarespace had not yet launched AI tools; the story has been updated.

articles.title_orig: Humiliated Putin’s Crisis Explodes in His Face
articles.title_zh: Humiliated Putin’s Crisis Explodes in His Face
articles.content_orig:
Vladimir Putinâs military planes are blowing up because of substandard imported fuel theyâre forced to use after the success of Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.
Ukrainian intelligence said on Friday that a Russian SU-57 fighter jet had crashed after engine problems at the Astrakhan regionâs Akhtubinsk airfield. Ukraine said the plane had likely malfunctioned because it had used the wrong kind of jet fuel.
âOne of the reasons why engines of this type can explode or suffer catastrophic failure is poor-quality fuel,â it said in a release.
Ukraine has spent months pummeling Russiaâs oil refineries with drone strikes.
The malfunction is an embarrassment for the Kremlin, as the SU-57, Russiaâs most advanced fighter jet, costs around $140 million.
Ukrainian intelligence added that the same kind of fuel is used to power other Russian fighter planes and airborne weapons key to its campaign in Ukraine, including the Geran 4 and 5 jet-powered drones.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
The agency pointed out that Russia is being forced to use fuel imported from countries including India, Egypt and South Korea following the success of long-range Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.
According to figures from the International Energy Agency , Ukraine has launched more than 300 attacks on Russian refineries this year, successfully striking more than two dozen. Late October and early November have seen a new wave of attacks. Over the weekend , Ukraine hit Russiaâs Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, setting it ablaze, as well as a refinery in the Samara region.
Ukraine claims to have knocked out half of Russiaâs refining capacity this year, causing front-line Russian fuel shortages in Ukraine. Russia is the worldâs third-largest oil producer, but in August imports rose to record levels amid the Ukrainian attacks. In response, Russia has banned aviation fuel exports.
Itâs one of several blowbacks Putin is facing over his Ukraine campaign, as domestic inflation spikes and long queues of motorists have been pictured at gas stations because of the fuel crisis.
Ukraineâs bombing campaign has enraged Trump, who has sought to pin blame on Ukraine for U.S. gas price increases, which are in fact caused by his war with Iran.
He has sought to pressure Ukraine into stopping the strikes, but Ukraine has resisted the pressure, launching new attacks in recent weeks.

articles.title_orig: As peacekeepers leave Western Sahara, refugees yearn to end a half-century wait
articles.title_zh: As peacekeepers leave Western Sahara, refugees yearn to end a half-century wait
articles.content_orig:
The conflict pits Morocco, which considers the region its own, against the Algeria-backed Polisario Front, which seeks a separate state
At 51, Binina Mohamed is as old as the conflict that drove her from the Western Sahara region into a refugee camp in southern Algeria, where she has spent her life among tens of thousands of others facing a similar fate.
The confrontation over her native land, often described as Africa’s longest-running territorial dispute, was brought back into focus this weekend by a UN Security ‌Council row that led to the end of a decades-old peacekeeping mission there.
The Western Sahara conflict pits Morocco, which considers the territory its own, against the Algeria-backed Polisario Front, a political and military organisation that has been seeking a separate state there since the departure of former colonial power Spain in 1976. Peacekeepers have watched over the territory since 1991, when the UN brokered a ceasefire ending years of guerrilla warfare between the two sides.

articles.title_orig: Judge allows class action McRib lawsuit against McDonald's to proceed - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Judge allows class action McRib lawsuit against McDonald's to proceed - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
A 'Barron's Roundtable' panel discusses how the fast-food chain will manage the pinch on consumers' wallets.
A federal judge ruled Friday that McDonald's must face a proposed class action lawsuit accusing the fast-food giant of misleading customers about the meat used in its popular McRib sandwich.
U.S. District Judge April Perry in Chicago rejected the company's bid to dismiss the lawsuit in its entirety, allowing consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment claims to proceed while dismissing five other claims without prejudice.
The lawsuit, filed by four consumers in December, alleges that McDonald's designed the McRib patty to resemble a rack of pork ribs despite containing no actual rib meat.
The plaintiffs argue that the sandwich's name, appearance and marketing mislead customers into believing they are purchasing a more expensive cut of pork.
MCDONALD'S HIT WITH LAWSUIT CLAIMING MCRIB CONTAINS NO REAL RIB MEAT
McDonald's must face a proposed class action lawsuit accusing the fast-food giant of misleading customers about the meat used in its popular McRib sandwich. (David Paul Morris/Getty Images, File / Getty Images)
Perry determined that it was too early to conclude that consumers could not reasonably expect the sandwich to contain rib meat, citing allegations about its marketing and consumer surveys submitted by the plaintiffs.
One survey found that 72% of respondents expected the McRib to contain rib meat, while another found that 67% considered rib meat important or very important to their purchasing decision, according to the court filing.
The ruling allows portions of the case to proceed but does not establish that McDonald's engaged in deceptive advertising.
NELSON PELTZ-LED GROUP OFFERS TO BUY WENDY’S FOR $1.4B
There are nearly 45,000 McDonald's restaurants worldwide. (Edgar Su/Reuters, File / Reuters Photos)
As FOX Business previously reported , the lawsuit alleges that the McRib contains lower-grade pork products, including pork shoulder, heart, tripe and stomach, rather than rib meat.
McDonald's has denied the allegations, maintaining that the sandwich contains 100% pork sourced from U.S. farmers and suppliers. The company previously told FOX Business that it does not use heart, tripe or scalded stomach in the McRib patty.
McDonald's argued that the sandwich's name does not mislead reasonable consumers and that its publicly available ingredient list identifies pork as the primary ingredient.
Perry rejected the argument that the McRib's trademarked name shields the company from deceptive marketing claims, noting that other McDonald's products, including the McChicken and Egg McMuffin, have names that describe their ingredients.
GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE
A representative for McDonald's did not immediately respond to FOX Business' request for comment.
Introduced in 1981, the McRib has developed a loyal following through its periodic limited-time returns to McDonald's menus. The sandwich features a boneless pork patty covered in barbecue sauce and topped with onions and pickles.
There are nearly 14,000 McDonald's restaurants in the U.S. and more than 45,000 worldwide.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
articles.title_zh: Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
articles.content_orig:
A new rule stops the model from rebuilding specific existing games, but developers say it also blocks their own projects.
Anthropic's Claude Code and the Opus 5.5 model have reportedly begun to refuse some tasks related to copying video games and reverse engineering, according to a recent report .
The refusals may be linked to a new rule that tells the model not to recreate a specific existing game. An X/Twitter user known as Chasm shared the alleged rule's text, which reads, "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." Developers are also complaining on GitHub that Claude Code stops game-related work, including projects they say are their own. Some users say it also refuses generic tasks, such as analyzing a crash dump or using the Reverse Engineer Anything tool.
Anthropic has not made a standalone announcement, but Tbreak reports that the company confirmed the change through a statement by one of its staff members. Two sentences were added to the Claude Code prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating other people's games, and the company says it will keep adjusting the balance. Original games, genre games, and projects made from the user's own designs and assets should still work.
The change comes as more AI-made game clones appear on Steam; for example, Steam Next Fest was reportedly flooded with them.

articles.title_orig: New CB90 CX Is Bigger, Optionally Crewed Evolution Of Saab’s Proven Combat Boat
articles.title_zh: New CB90 CX Is Bigger, Optionally Crewed Evolution Of Saab’s Proven Combat Boat
articles.content_orig:
Home » Saab unveils optionally crewed CB90 CX ahead of Euronaval 2026
Saab has unveiled a larger, optionally crewed variant of its Combat Boat 90 (CB90) fast assault craft designed to expand the role of the combat boat beyond troop transport to a multimission combat platform.
The new variant, known as CB90 Capability X (CB90 CX), will initially be offered in three configurations: intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), anti-ship warfare, and short-range air-defence (SHORAD).
Sweden is the launch customer, and the first boat is undergoing final acceptance trials ahead of delivery.
Briefing media online on 30 October, Anders Hellman, head of Saab’s business unit Docksta, said CB90 CX was the company’s response to a rapidly changing maritime security environment, where naval forces need to detect threats earlier, distribute capability across more platforms, and operate with greater flexibility.
He pointed to incidents involving critical infrastructure in the Baltic Sea, the use of small distributed systems against conventional naval forces in the Black Sea, and attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea.
“These are of course different environments, but I think the lesson is similar,” he said. “Naval forces need to see more, they have to move faster, and most importantly, they need to distribute their capabilities across more platforms. So, the idea is quite simple: we have taken a proven combat boat and turned it into a distributed capability.”
With an overall length of 18 m, a beam of 4 m, and a draught of 1.1 m, CB90 CX is 1.4 m longer and 0.3 m wider than the CB90 Next Generation (NG) variant. Powered by two 1,100 hp engines driving waterjets, the boat has a top speed of more than 40 kt fully loaded and a range of more than 300 n miles at around 40 kt. It can carry a crew complement of up to 10 personnel.
According to Hellman, the larger hull has increased payload capacity by more than 50% compared with CB90 NG, on a like-for-like basis, from around 3 tonnes to “well beyond” 5 tonnes. It has also significantly improved seakeeping, he said. The boat is built to the DNV HSLC R2 class notation, which enables it to operate up to 100 n miles from a safe haven in summer and 50 n miles in winter. “From a Baltic perspective, this gives us free manoeuvrability within the entire Baltic,” he said.
Asked by Naval News whether the larger hull had required any trade-offs, Hellman said the company had been able “to keep the same user experience and feel” of the baseline vessel, which is centred around simplicity of design, and ease of use and operation. He added that the profile of the vessel has been kept low, both to limit its signature and to ensure it remains transportable by road and air.
More significant than the hull changes, according to Hellman, is the vessel’s new common system architecture, known as Combat Core. This integrates ship automation, platform monitoring, fire control, and a new steer-by-wire system into a single digital backbone, enabling capabilities to be added and upgraded throughout the boat’s lifecycle. The Combat Core is based on an open architecture, allowing customers to integrate their own sensors and weapons.
Saab’s Autonomous Ocean Core software is integrated with the Combat Core to provide the basis for uncrewed operations. According to Hellman, all CB90 CX boats are prepared for uncrewed operations from the outset, enabling the boat to be controlled from a remote station or through AI functionality. “This doesn’t take people out of the decision-making process, but it gives the operators much better flexibility in how they use people and platforms,” he noted.
Saab is initially producing the CB90 CX in three customer-driven configurations, although Hellman stressed these are only a starting point.
The ISR configuration is equipped with a Saab Sea Giraffe 1X X-band 3D surveillance radar, which rotates at 60 rpm to provide 360-degree coverage of air and surface targets and has an air detection range of more than 100 km. The radar sits on a newly designed mast that extends to 11 m, enabling the boat to see over islands in the archipelago. In its lowest 4 m position the mast allows unrestricted operations at speed. A Saab Trackfire remote weapon station armed with a 12.7 mm or 30 mm gun provides counter-uncrewed aerial system protection.
The anti-ship version was shown during the briefing armed with MBDA’s Marte ER sea-skimming fire-and-forget missile, which has a range or more than 100 km with external targeting data. Amphibious forces have traditionally carried missile teams ashore to set up and engage naval targets. With the missile system onboard, “the combat boat can do more than transport the capability. It becomes part of the strike capability itself,” Hellman said, adding that it also enables forces to regroup much faster and with greater manoeuvrability. He noted that Sweden’s amphibious battalion is acquiring a different missile, and that the Marte ER fit is intended to demonstrate the platform’s flexibility.
The SHORAD variant is armed with Rheinmetall’s Seasnake 30 naval gun, which fires KCE-30 30 x 173 mm ammunition. Its primary targets are helicopters, drones, and loitering munitions, with ground targets, small landing craft, and small patrol boats as secondary targets. In February 2026 FMV, Sweden’s defence procurement agency, ordered an initial eight Seasnake 30 systems to arm its CB90s under the Amphibious Battalion 2030 modernisation programme. “The big change is that short-range air defence becomes mobile; it can move and appear when it is needed,” Hellman said.
He said the three configurations are intended to work together, operating in different locations but connected as one force, taking the combat boat “from carrying the fighting force to becoming part of it”.
Saab is also developing additional capabilities for CB90 CX, including the option to launch drones – with both tube-launched systems and quadcopters under consideration – and torpedoes. Hellman said the company has a parallel development track for further configurations.
Sweden has a total of 36 CB90s on order, including 10 ordered in June 2024, 22 in 2025, and a further four added in the first half of 2026.
The CB90 CX will be offered alongside the CB90 NG, which Saab will keep in production. To meet anticipated demand, the company is building a new site at Docksta that will double its production capacity. Hellman said its focus markets are NATO and allied nations, particularly in the Baltic and Mediterranean regions. More than 300 CB90s are in service with nine navies.

articles.title_orig: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?
articles.title_zh: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?
articles.content_orig:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to overhaul immigration rules.
Proposals to change the requirements to qualify for permanent settlement in the UK were first outlined in detail in November 2025, when Mahmood was home secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government.
Following a consultation , Mahmood has now announced her final decision on what changes should be taken forward.
Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) – also known as settlement – gives someone the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.
Under the current system, people with ILR can also apply for benefits if they are eligible.
People who have lived in the UK for 12 months after being given ILR can apply for British citizenship, if they also meet other requirements .
Under the government's plans, the standard length of time migrants will have to live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement will double from five to 10 years.
Under this 10-year pathway, applicants must have earned at least £12,571 for five of the seven years immediately before being granted settlement.
However, there will be a shorter qualifying period of five years for certain groups, including:
People earning over £125,141 a year, as well as "highly skilled" migrants such as those on Global Talent or Innovator Founder visas, will qualify after three years.
Migrants who have claimed certain benefits or breached immigration rules will only be able to settle after at least 20 years.
To qualify for settlement, migrants will also have to meet other conditions including:
There will be a different set of rules for refugees – people who have been granted asylum in the UK because they are unable to return to their own country as they fear persecution.
Refugees who arrived in the UK through an official government scheme will qualify for settlement after five years.
However, other refugees will need to wait 10 years and either work or study.
Those who do not work or study will need to wait 20 years.
Refugees who arrived in the UK by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they don't.
The changes will apply to migrants who are already in the UK but not those who have already been granted settlement.
A partner who arrives with someone who then applies for ILR will be able to settle at the same time, as long as they meet the relevant requirements.
However, a partner who joins later will need to complete the same qualifying residence period before they are eligible for settlement.
Eligible couples will be able to combine their earnings to meet the minimum income  requirement.
The household income threshold will be £25,142 – twice the individual minimum income requirement.
Children under 18 will continue to be able to settle with their parents.
They will be exempt from the income, government debt, English language and Life in the UK test requirements, but will remain subject to the relevant suitability and criminality requirements.
Young adults aged 18 to 24, who remain dependant on their family, will also continue to be able to settle alongside them.
They will be expected to meet all the adult mandatory requirements but not the individual income requirement.
Someone who is aged 25 or over when their family becomes eligible for settlement will be expected to qualify independently.
Eligible partners, parents and children of British citizens will continue to qualify for settlement after five years.

articles.title_orig: China Tech Stocks Get Fresh Lifeline From Beijing
articles.title_zh: China Tech Stocks Get Fresh Lifeline From Beijing
articles.content_orig:
Alibaba BABA , JD.com JD and PDD Holdings PDD moved higher in U.S. premarket trading Monday after Chinese regulators signaled a fresh effort to stabilize the country's battered stock market.
The move follows an 8.5% October drop in the CSI 300 , its worst monthly performance since early 2016. The benchmark had also fallen for 12 consecutive weeks, according to TipRanks.
Beijing is now stepping in with more liquidity.
The People's Bank of China said it will conduct a new swap operation Tuesday that could inject more than 100 billion yuan, or roughly $15 billion , into the equity market. Thirty-one brokerages and fund companies have already applied for quotas worth more than 100 billion yuan.
The swap facility allows securities firms, insurers and fund managers to exchange eligible assets for more liquid central-bank assets, giving them additional capacity to buy stocks.
China is also making its relending program for share repurchases and stake increases a long-term mechanism , while cutting the program's interest rate to 1% from 1.25% .
Regulators are applying pressure directly as well.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission urged major index constituents and leading technology companies to actively buy back shares , while also encouraging newer ETFs and fund managers to increase equity exposure during the downturn. Officials are separately studying whether to ease margin rules to improve market liquidity.
The policy response helped lift sentiment Monday, with the Shanghai Composite gaining 1.1% and the CSI 300 also moving higher.
Alibaba, JD and PDD have been caught in the broader decline as investors grapple with weak Chinese consumption, persistent property-sector problems and pressure across technology shares.
I think the key point here is that Beijing is sending a clearer message that it does not want the equity selloff to spiral.
For Alibaba, JD and PDD, that matters because their stocks have increasingly been trading on macro sentiment and policy risk, not just company fundamentals.
The latest measures can improve liquidity and potentially put a floor under sentiment.
But they do not fix the underlying issues by themselves.
China still needs stronger consumption, better economic momentum and more confidence in corporate earnings for the rally to become durable.
For investors, the key things to watch are how much of the new liquidity is actually deployed, whether corporate buybacks accelerate, and whether China follows these market-support steps with broader fiscal or economic stimulus .
The immediate signal is supportive.
The harder question is whether Beijing can turn that support into a lasting recovery.

articles.content_orig:

Microsoft's COO Helen Chiang was fired from Xbox a few weeks ago, after 27 years of top-level leadership spent across the org, most prolifically at Minecraft.
The removal was abrupt and somewhat confusing on the face of it. Chiang was widely respected across the Microsoft stack and is a trusted figure, described to me as "by the book" by our own sources. When it emerged that she had been fired for "policy violations," it added an unexpected twist that left us with more questions than answers, ultimately.
Now, Helen Chiang has responded to the incident on LinkedIn , titled "Clarity is Kindness," which is a comment Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made to the WSJ while discussing the health of Microsoft's gaming business recently.
There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate," Chiang writes, "silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight."
In the full post shared below, Chiang denies that she leaked information, sought employment at Microsoft competitors, engaged in insider trading, bullying, or embezzlement, or that she left because she didn't get the CEO job. She says that she always hoped to stay at Microsoft and "keep building," and this departure wasn't what she envisioned.
" I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal."
As to not paraphrase, I've included the full text from the post below.
UPDATE (November 2, 2026): Note here about the "Nelson-level" scandal: this does not refer to Xbox's Major Nelson as some have speculated , who by all accounts is a lovely and upstanding dude (including my own account here). This actually refers to an internal Microsoft meme. Microsoft's internal training videos feature a fictional dude called Nelson, who was placed in a bunch of hypothetical scenarios to train Microsoft employees on proper conduct. Microsoft has been required to have these videos (which I'm told are of surprisingly high production value) since Microsoft fell afoul of anti-competition laws during the Clinton administration in times of yore.
There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight. First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story. Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here. Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record. Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I’ve been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven’t actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July. I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously. I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind. To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we’ve shared over the past 20 years and the impact we’ve had on one another. Some of you I haven’t been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I’ve never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work. This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story." — Helen Chiang, former Xbox COO.
Helen Chiang's somewhat unceremonious departure comes amidst widespread upheaval at Xbox as Microsoft restructures its gaming org , which has led to thousands of layoffs, divestitures, and studio closures. Microsoft managed to return some studios to independent ownership and has sold others to publishers, as it tries to rein in spending in general.
The Coalition has been put on the hook for $500 million per Microsoft's finance auditors, who only see the dollars and not the complexity of game development, the impact the pandemic had on the development of games between Gears 5 and E-Day, and other mitigating factors.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has returned the brand's focus to its core customers in recent months, with a return of exclusive games, boosting investment in the existing console infrastructure, and improving things on the back end for game developers.
I suspect there'll be more disruption before things calm down ... as the industry in general reels from an overabundance of content, reduced consumer spending, and the AI -fostered RAMpocalypse .

Jez is known for breaking exclusive news and analysis as relates to the Microsoft ecosystem — while being powered by tea. articles.title_orig: How China Might Target US Midterms - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.title_zh: How China Might Target US Midterms - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
articles.content_orig:
No research shows Chinese propaganda or disinformation playing a pivotal role in the midterm elections, particularly when compared to Russia’s aggressive attempts. Yet significant blind spots exist. If it desired, Beijing is well-positioned to shape political debate through the WeChat app and through Chinese AI models.
Rather than shifting control of Congress, Beijing’s goal would likely be to reduce the presence of known Communist Party critics, particularly those serving in the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Created by Congress in October 2000, the Commission monitors Chinese human rights and rule of law.
Several competitive races feature Commission members, including former Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio and current Commission Chair Dan Sullivan in Alaska. House races in Iowa and Virginia involve current Commission members Zach Nunn and Jen Kiggans. Ashley Hinson, who is running for the Senate in Iowa, is on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, another Congressional body critical of the regime.
Texas looks particularly sensitive for a different reason. WeChat , a messaging and multi-function app, has an estimated 1.5 million US users, concentrated in states with large Chinese American populations. Chinese Americans make up roughly one percent of Texas’s population .
Chinese state-sponsored censorship on WeChat is well-documented. A 2025 University of Texas study based on interviews with 20 Chinese Americans in Texas detailed how political misinformation circulates on the platform. One young interviewee described how her father read that an Asian American woman had been elected mayor of Boston months before the actual election.
“He just accepts everything he reads, and then he just forwards it,” she said. “My mother-in-law, too.”
Cultural and social pressures reduce willingness to correct misinformation in family or friend groups. “It doesn’t feel right for me to talk bad to my elders, especially in the group chat setting,” a 19-year-old Chinese American explained.
In this environment, the app is powerful. “A lot of people don’t know who to vote for, so they are easily swayed,” another interviewee commented. “It is a big political platform, and a lot of people will just blindly follow.”
The 2026 elections are the first to take place in an environment where AI chatbots are widely available. About one-fifth of Americans plan to use AI tools to help learn about candidates or inform voting decisions, according to a recent survey . Most will turn to American models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Perplexity, but many US developers are increasingly relying on Chinese-origin models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, allowing them to enter the US information environment.
These models reflect the Chinese government’s official stances on domestic politics and human rights. Censorship and propaganda have also been found in responses to questions about US press freedom and elections.
One study examined Chinese AI models’ responses to questions about the upcoming US elections. Conducted by a research group based in Europe, researchers tested seven AI models (five US and two Chinese) with a set of 20 polling-style questions.
All models proved relatively consistent and offered mixed results in terms of partisan preferences. The two Chinese models did not diverge sharply from their US counterparts in their responses. DeepSeek, for example, selected the Democratic option on two questions about which party’s candidate it would select for Congress and which party it prefers to control Congress. So did Claude and Perplexity (99% on one of the questions). By contrast, Qwen chose Democrats 55% and 75% of the time, respectively.
The results are striking for what they show about the leeway allowed the Chinese models to comment on US versus Chinese politics. DeepSeek offered critical assessments of the US president’s job performance. Asking the same questions about Chinese President Xi Jinping would almost certainly produce refusals or strictly glowing reviews.
Major holes remain in our understanding of where and how Chinese Communist Party-linked electoral influence could be occurring. Researchers, election monitors, and others focused on election integrity should address these gaps — particularly before the 2028 elections.
Sarah Cook is founder of China Rights Analytics and Advising LLC and author of the UnderReported China newsletter.

articles.title_orig: 'Exceptionally horrific strike' — Russian bombs hit school used as humanitarian aid center in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, killing 26
articles.title_zh: 'Exceptionally horrific strike' — Russian bombs hit school used as humanitarian aid center in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, killing 26
articles.content_orig:
Video shows smoke rising from Komyshuvakha blast crater
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".
Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.
He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.
The Russian military has not publicly commented.
There are fears that the death toll will rise further as a number of people are still under the rubble
Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.
In his video address late on Monday, Zelensky said 26 people were now known to have died.
He earlier said that "the Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week" on Monday.
"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."
He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky during a temporary ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".
"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.
The Russian strikes left a huge crater where Ukrainian officials say people were sheltering
Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".
He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.
A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Teams from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume peace talks in the next few days after negotiations were suspended in February, with Moscow stepping up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.
However, no major breakthrough is expected at the talks that are likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates.

articles.title_orig: Chili’s customers in North Carolina suffer burns after sipping margaritas mistakenly made with cleaning chemical
articles.title_zh: Chili’s customers in North Carolina suffer burns after sipping margaritas mistakenly made with cleaning chemical
articles.content_orig:
A Chili’s Grill & Bar in North Carolina is back in business after three customers and two workers suffered chemical burns on their mouths from sipping margaritas mistakenly made with a cleaning chemical last week.
The eatery in Forest City was shut down on Thursday after the customers, who had ordered the drinks shortly after the restaurant opened for lunch, “immediately experienced discomfort and chemical burns in and around their mouths,” the Foothills Health District said in a statement.
“Two restaurant employees subsequently tasted the substance and reported similar symptoms,” the FHD statement.
It was reopened the next day after local health inspectors discovered that a worker “preparing the bar for lunch service discovered the unlabeled container and, believing its contents to be sugar, used the chemical to prepare the margarita station.”
Chili’s, according to its menu , offers several margaritas that are make with a “citrus-sugar rimmer” in addition to the traditional salt.
FHD spokesperson Megan Rollins said in an email the investigation was closed and no fines were issued. She said the injured parties received medical treatment, but had no information about their conditions.
A Chili’s spokesperson said in an email that this was an “incident isolated to a single restaurant in Forest City, North Carolina, that resulted in injuries to two of our guests and Team Members.”
“Our team took immediate action to support those affected and avoid further injuries,” the spokesperson said. “We have thoroughly investigated the circumstances and addressed the issues specific to this location.”
The spokesperson did not respond to a follow-up question from NBC News seeking an explanation for why their tally of injured customers was different from the one provided earlier by the FHD.
This Chili’s is located about 60 miles west of Charlotte, North Carolina.
On the morning of Oct. 26, according to the FHD statement, “a restaurant employee received a granulated degreasing chemical from a contracted worker who was power washing the exterior, and placed it into an unlabeled container.”
For reasons unclear, “the container was brought inside the restaurant and left in the bar area.”
Two days later, those chemicals were inadvertently added to margaritas.
Corky Siemaszko is a senior reporter for NBC News Digital.

Halloween is in the rearview mirror. Next stop: Black Friday sales, which have started earlier than ever, creeping in the first week of November and lasting the entire month. That's good news for those of you who hemmed and hawed on a big tech buy during Prime Day in October. You still have time to score best-of-the-year pricing from Beats, Bose, Amazon, Apple and nearly every other major brand, plus plenty of minor ones.
Instead of waiting until my post-turkey nap, I rounded up the best tech deals now. That way you're not refreshing deal pages at the Thanksgiving table. Better yet, buy those headphones you've had your eye on now and you can just sit back and enjoy some noise-cancelling silence on the flight to see family.
AirPods Pro 3 ($199, was $249) Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus ($40, was $70) Apple iPad 11-inch (A16) ($399, was $449) Ring Battery Doorbell 2K ($40, was $99) Apple AirTags (2nd Gen) 4-pack ($80, was $99)
Black Friday always falls on the day after Thanksgiving, which this year is Friday, Nov. 27. It used to be a one-day event, but these days, anyone calling it a single-day sale is either lying or completely out of touch. Most major retailers will roll out discounts weeks in advance — think of it as "Black November." That means you'll want to start keeping tabs on prices now, and who knows? You might be done with all of your holiday shopping before the turkey coma hits.
Not necessarily everything , but pretty dang close. We're already seeing close to record-low prices on TVs, laptops and headphones, and it's common to see gaming consoles and appliances go on sale too.
Pretty much. The usual suspects — Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Macy's, Kohl's, Wayfair, The Home Depot — will all go big. Smaller brands often join in too, though some do it quietly (think: an unadvertised 20% off code hidden at checkout). Others, like REI, make a point to not have a sale with the rest of them, instead opting for earlier sales. The point is, if you're shopping online at all this fall, there's no excuse to pay full price.
Have a plan (or even better, a spreadsheet): Ever end up overspending while grocery shopping when you don't have a list? Me too. Don't wait until the week of Thanksgiving (or later) to decide what to buy. Create a wishlist and track prices starting now. Once that dream TV, laptop or pair of noise-cancelling headphones drops to a real all-time low, jump on it — good deals don't linger.
Do your homework: Don't rely on a single retailer. In most cases, it pays to shop around. Prices also tend to fluctuate, so don't assume the first small markdown you see is the best one.
Be skeptical: Here's a dirty little secret: Some "sales" aren't really sales. Retailers bump prices before big events so the discount looks steeper. Web tools like Honey or CamelCamelCamel can show you price history (to see if that 95% off gadget has ever sold at MSRP), but if you don't feel like going full spreadsheet mode, I'll be doing that work for you all month long — rounding up legit deals, not the fake ones.
These infinitely useful little trackers will help make sure you don’t lose your keys, wallet, bag or jacket ever again (though you may need an accessory to attach them to your stuff).
This is the second generation of Apple's Bluetooth tracker. This time around, the ring is louder and the range is longer. Check out Yahoo's second-gen AirTag review for more.
The latest AirPods Pro came out last October, and Apple skipped a Pro update at September's iPhone 18 event, even as it unveiled the new AirPods 5 . Frankly, these didn’t need an upgrade. They deliver the most effective noise cancellation of any Apple earbuds — something I can personally confirm. When I take them to a noisy coffee shop to work, they shut out so much of the commotion that it can feel like I’m working in a library.
In Yahoo Tech’s review , our reviewer praised the great sound and improved eight-hour battery life. They also pack heart-rate sensing for workouts and make hands-free Siri surprisingly useful: You can even nod or shake your head to answer questions, including whether you want to take an incoming call.
In Yahoo's guide to the best tablets , we named this standard iPad model the ideal choice for most folks. It uses the A16 chip, which isn't quite powerful enough to support Apple Intelligence . But if you don't need those features, you'll get an iPad that's able to handle all your browsing and streaming needs as well as helping you get some work done.
Great time to buy: This is just a buck above the lowest price we've seen since Apple enacted its price hikes earlier this year.
If you're looking for the best tech item under $50, you've found it. For about the price of a couple of movie tickets and a popcorn, the Fire TV Stick 4K offers quick and easy access to more content than you'll ever be able to watch in a lifetime. We're talking 1.5 million shows and movies at your fingertips. And right now, you can snag it for 50% off.
Don't have a 4K TV? The HD version is also on sale.
This is the newest model of the Ring Battery Doorbell. It doesn't need to be wired into your wall, so you have more flexibility on where to put it. It shoots 2K resolution video and has up to a 6x zoom. There's a two-way speaker and microphone so you can hear and speak to whoever comes to your door. Just note that you'll need a Ring Protect subscription to save clips and use the AI-enhanced person detection.
Attention, "Roomba-or-nothing" folks: Having any sort of robovac is great, but you know what's really handy? One that doubles as a mop so it can clean every type of floor in your house. This model boasts as much as 70% more suction power than other iRobot vacuums, and it's smart enough to avoid carpets and rugs when it's in mopping mode.
Great time to buy: This price is just about as low as it's been in the past year, aside from one quick dip back in April.
Thinking about installing a USB-outlet? Consider this surge-protecting outlet instead. You get five outlets plus four more USB charging ports (three USB type A and one USB-C). Plus, it'll screw into the center of your outlet so you don't yank it off the wall every time you unplug something. Safe. Secure. Inexpensive. Sold!
Many brands claim their robot vacuums have an auto-emptying dock for hands-off maintenance, but this model actually walks the walk. Its dust bag can hold up to 90 days' worth of dirt and debris, plus the dock refills the robot's water tank and washes and heat-dries its mop pads, so you don't have to lift a finger.
The MacBook Air was once Apple's more affordable laptop. But with the addition of the Neo this March, the Air now sits as the middle child in the MacBook lineup. That makes sense — the MacBook Air never felt like a budget model. It's a fully realized, very capable and plenty powerful MacBook that'll work well for all but the most demanding users. (Unless you plan to throw lots of 3D animation rendering or AI model building at your laptop, you probably don't need to upgrade to the Pro model.)
Great time to buy: This is the lowest Amazon price we've seen in three months.
Mario Kart is one of Nintendo's most popular game series — and for good reason. Mario Kart World is the most expansive (and expensive) game yet and has received high marks since its June 2025 release. It's also only available for the Switch 2, meaning it isn't compatible with older Switch models.

articles.title_orig: Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
articles.title_zh: Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
articles.content_orig:
Crude oil prices fell sharply Monday as the presidents of the U.S. and Iran signalled they are open to a diplomatic solution to the conflict that has disrupted energy markets for eight months.
U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures shed 7.4% to close at $96.46 a barrel, the biggest daily loss since July 27. Brent crude , the international benchmark, lost 7.6% to settle at $104.77 a barrel.
President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that Iran wants to "make a deal and that could happen." U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said over the weekend that Trump prefers not to use military force against Iran and would like to resolve the conflict diplomatically.
Trump has previously said that he will not attack Iran before the U.S. midterms. But the oil market had priced in the risk of a major military escalation after the elections, gaining more than 10% in October.
The oil market has sold off during previous phases of the war on rumors of a possible settlement, only for the conflict to subsequently escalate and spike prices again.
Trump "hasn't made a decision" on whether to strike Iran again, Rubio told reporters.
"What the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," the secretary of State said. "But we would prefer to do it peacefully."
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran is seeking to resolve problems through dialogue, according to state-owned Islamic Republic News Agency . Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has granted the government certain authorities to do this, Pezeshkian said.
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said an agreement with the U.S. is possible if Washington "demonstrates goodwill" and is "truly seeking a peaceful solution," according to IRNA.
Araghchi said mediators are discussing the proposal Iran made during the United Nations General Assembly in September. Tehran expects the U.S. to lift sanctions, reduce its military presence in the region to previous levels and lift the blockade, the foreign minister said.
But Khamenei on Saturday called for Tehran's armed forces to meet "any level or type of threat" with "an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response."
Reports about diplomatic efforts will have a big impact on crude oil prices because much of the market's recent gains were risk premium in anticipation of a possible escalation, according to Ryan McKay, director of commodity strategy at TD Securities.
"With that said, so long as there is no concrete conclusion to the war, and tanker and Houthi attacks remain prevalent, we do not anticipate a complete erosion of the risk premium via diplomacy headlines alone," McKay said.
— CNBC's Lim Hui Jie contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: China Is Sending AI-Powered Robots Into the Ocean to Uncover Its Lost Ancient History
articles.title_zh: China Is Sending AI-Powered Robots Into the Ocean to Uncover Its Lost Ancient History
articles.content_orig:
China's next five-year archaeological plan, covering 2026 to 2030 , proposes deploying artificial intelligence, ancient-DNA analysis, remote sensing and deep-sea robots across some of the country's most significant historical sites. The program is designed to recover artifacts, reconstruct damaged objects and investigate questions about human migration, early states and maritime trade that conventional excavation has so far left only partially answered.
Excavations routinely produce large quantities of broken, scattered material whose connections are difficult to establish manually. Specialized AI systems would identify artifact fragments, match pieces to one another and generate virtual restorations , allowing researchers to study an object's probable original appearance without physically altering the surviving material.
Each pillar of the plan addresses a distinct limitation of conventional archaeological methods.
Remote sensing , which uses aerial or satellite data to detect buried structures, could help researchers locate remains before excavation begins. Ancient-DNA analysis would contribute to population research, tracing relationships, migrations and environmental adaptation among communities that lived thousands of years ago. Usable results require biological material preserved well enough to avoid contamination.
Underwater robotics addresses sites that human divers cannot safely reach. The plan calls for purpose-built deep-sea robots , specialized diving equipment and precision excavation tools aimed at shipwrecks and Maritime Silk Road routes lying on the seabed.
Institutionally, the program is intended to be permanent rather than a series of isolated projects. The official plan describes a national-level archaeological laboratory and a maritime-archaeology hub in Qingdao, signaling an effort to embed high-technology research into standing infrastructure.
Named sites and international partnerships give the blueprint a concrete geographic scope.
Research targets extend from northern China's earliest known sites through the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and across Eurasia. Among the domestic priorities is the transition from Paleolithic hunter-gatherer life to agriculture and settled communities along the Yellow River, Yangtze River and southern Lingnan region.
Major Bronze Age and early-state sites, including Sanxingdui , Erlitou and Yinxu, feature prominently alongside historical infrastructure such as the Qin dynasty Direct Road, the Great Wall and the Grand Canal. International partnerships with institutions in Egypt, Greece, Saudi Arabia and Tunisia are planned for comparative research, underwater surveys and heritage preservation.
The Nanhai No. 1 shows what underwater excavation can recover and what it demands in return.
The Nanhai No. 1 , a Southern Song-era merchant vessel associated with trade between China and overseas markets, illustrates why underwater archaeology occupies a central place in the new blueprint. Discovered in 1987 and raised intact in 2007, the wreck was transferred to a purpose-built aquatic environment at the Guangdong Maritime Silk Road Museum, where conservation and excavation continue under controlled conditions.
UNESCO describes the site as unusually valuable because its preservation captures cargo and food remains that document commerce and daily life aboard the vessel. According to a government-linked report, more than 180,000 cultural relics have been salvaged and preserved from the site.
Ambition and evidence are not the same thing, and the plan's limits deserve equal billing.
AI cannot reconstruct information the surviving evidence does not support; a virtual restoration is only as reliable as the fragments behind it. Deep-sea robots still contend with pressure, poor visibility, currents and fragile materials.
Ancient-DNA results depend on preservation conditions and rigorous contamination controls, and their interpretation requires care. None of this invalidates the program's potential, but discovery and conclusion are not the same thing.
The blueprint's stated cultural objectives are as significant as its scientific ones, and they invite scrutiny.
The plan carries an explicit cultural objective alongside its scientific aims: increasing China's international influence over interpretations of its history and civilization. That goal raises practical questions about data access, interpretive independence and the terms under which foreign institutions will participate. How those questions are answered will determine whether the international partnerships function as genuine scholarly collaboration or primarily serve a national framing agenda. Those details remain unclear and will merit close attention as the program moves from blueprint to fieldwork.
