articles.title_orig: Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang denies violating Microsoft policies in parting LinkedIn post
articles.title_zh: Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang denies violating Microsoft policies in parting LinkedIn post
articles.content_orig:
Asha Sharma Helen Chiang Microsoft Xbox
Helen Chiang had been at Microsoft since 2005. She spent over a decade overseeing Minecraft , the company’s most important gaming franchise, and survived this year’s big Xbox “reset” with a promotion to the role of the gaming division’s chief operating officer. Barely three months later, she’s suddenly out at the company she called home for more than two decades, a development which generated tons of speculation about whether she was fired or not. Chiang now says she’s breaking her silence to set the record straight.
“There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was ‘fired for a policy violation,'” she wrote on LinkedIn , referencing a report last month from Eurogamer alleging she was fired for a “ policy violation .” “That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight.”
Chiang went on to say that she never leaked confidential company information to the press or went outside of company-authorized communication channels. She said she also did not leave the company for a competitor, nor did she “engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity.” Chiang added that her past results and record speak for themselves, and that she did not leave the company because she’d been passed over for a bigger role. The chief operating officer role had not been something she’d lobbied for.
“I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others,” she wrote. “Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously. I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind.”
“We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” a spokesperson for Microsoft previously told Kotaku regarding Chiang’s departure. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”
The sudden move comes amid a massive reorganization of Xbox that has seen massive layoffs and studio divestitures as Microsoft seeks to rebuild the platform while also improving its bottom line. As chief operating officer, Chiang would have had a central role in helping to restructure and better optimize the tech giant’s gaming business ahead of the next console generation, Project Helix, which is reportedly set to arrive in 2028. Though the Xbox veteran set out to clear the air amid much of the recent speculation about her departure from the company, it’s still not clear what exactly happened.
“For the first time, we are establishing a Chief Operating Officer with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services,” Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote back in July . “Helen Chiang has been promoted to this role and will report directly to me. Over nearly two decades at XBOX, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from XBOX Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”
Sharma later told The Wall Street Journal “ clarity is kindness ” when describing the tough choices she was making to set the stage for an ambitious future. “Clarity is Kindness” is also how Chiang began her LinkedIn post today. “This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end,” she wrote. “And it is not the whole story.”

articles.title_zh: SpaceX Is Reportedly Looking At Buying Boost Mobile Or Using Its Cell Network
articles.content_orig:
The potential deal could serve as a shortcut to establishing SpaceX as a mobile carrier.
SpaceX may have found a potential path to circumvent its way into the mobile carrier industry via Boost Mobile. As first reported by The Washington Post , Elon Musk's company has held talks with Boost Mobile's parent company, EchoStar, in recent months that could see SpaceX launch "its own signature wireless service" through the existing network.
According to Washington Post 's sources, the deal could look like SpaceX acquiring Boost Mobile outright or gaining access to its cell network, which is leased from AT&T and T-Mobile. There could be a major hitch with the deal though, since SpaceX's potential mobile service would need the green light from those major mobile carriers, according to the report. The Washington Post also reported that major cell companies, which include AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon, have already turned down Musk down for access to its cell networks in order to launch a separate SpaceX service.
No deal has been confirmed yet, but the talks between SpaceX and EchoStar shouldn't be surprising for anyone paying attention to the company's recent dealings. Last year SpaceX acquired $2.6 billion worth of spectrum licenses from EchoStar, which would be used to improve its Starlink network's 5G connections. More recently, Starlink confirmed its plans to become a "major mobile carrier in the US" and made another major acquisition in the hopes of achieving that goal.

articles.title_orig: Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push
articles.title_zh: Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push
articles.content_orig:
China sales fell 31% last quarter, yet Mercedes says it is “indispensable” and plans to build future Chinese-market cars almost entirely with local parts.
2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA 220 Hybrid in Manufaktur Patagonia Red
Mercedes-Benz , though currently struggling to retain market position in China, says it will give a broader 2030 strategy update, which will include a detailed review of its China business, next year. The numbers explain the urgency: German brands have been getting crushed in China .
Mercedes-Benz is doubling down on the market that is hurting it most. According to Reuters , CEO Ola Källenius calls China an “indispensable market and innovation hub.
Third-quarter Mercedes-Benz Cars sales fell 8 percent to 407,232, with China down 31 percent to 86,800, according to BigGo . Elsewhere, Europe was up 5 percent, Germany was up 13 percent, and the US was up 6 percent, with record battery-electric sales up 61 percent. Adjusted return on sales for cars dropped to 2.5 percent from 4.8 percent, and Mercedes cut its full-year guidance to 2-3 percent from 3-5 percent; its CFO called the fourth quarter “a break-even quarter.”
Starting with the electric E-Class in the second half of 2027, Källenius said Mercedes will source “almost everything” in China for Chinese production. According to reports, CFO Harald Wilhelm also wants the company to rely less on China as a profit source. That is a split-screen strategy: stay in the world’s largest car market, but with local suppliers and less exposure to its price war. Mercedes has already felt that pain from tariffs and China’s EV boom.
If you live in the US, this is the good-news part. The China sourcing applies to cars built for China, and nothing in the reporting says it changes what’s sold here. What matters more is where Mercedes is growing: US sales rose 6 percent last quarter, and Källenius said the company plans further US investments and sees potential to lift annual sales from more than 300,000 vehicles toward 400,000, per Reuters. Audi announced a $4 billion US assembly plant that will create around 4,500 jobs. Mercedes too is changing gears in a push for higher volume after years of sliding sales. For buyers, that could mean more attention and more incentives, though nothing has been promised.
In Germany, Mercedes will relaunch a voluntary severance program for indirect staff from December. It booked about €1.8 billion (about $2 billion) in provisions for the last round in 2025, with most of the new program’s earnings impact expected in 2027. Källenius said further German investment depends on productivity and costs, noting US labor costs run at roughly 80 percent of German levels.

articles.title_orig: Karl Bushby ends 28-year journey at mother's house in Hull
articles.title_zh: Karl Bushby ends 28-year journey at mother's house in Hull
articles.content_orig:
A British adventurer has completed a 28-year walking journey around the world, arriving at his childhood home after travelling some 50,000km (31,070 miles) across jungles, frozen seas and international borders.
Karl Bushby, 57, was embraced by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house in Hull, northern England, on Monday, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”.
Hundreds of cheering supporters had welcomed him in the city centre before he made the final stretch home.
“Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the crowd. “Is that it, is it done?”
Bushby began what became known as his Goliath Expedition in Punta Arenas, southern Chile, in November 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a cheap plastic camera.
His goal was to reach his home city by an unbroken route, without using motorised transport to advance his journey.
The route took him north through the Americas, across the ice of the Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia, and onwards through Mongolia and China. He later swam across the Caspian Sea before continuing towards Europe.
Along the way, he negotiated the dense jungle of the Darien Gap between Colombia and Panama, was detained after entering Russia, and faced repeated visa and funding problems.
The global financial crisis in 2008 cost him major sponsors, adding to delays that stretched what he had expected to be a 12-year journey into 28 years.
Last month, he finally swam across the English Channel, clearing the last major obstacle before beginning the final walk home.
“They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said as he arrived in Hull. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.”
A feature-length documentary about his journey is in production, while Bushby plans to begin a speaking tour around England in the coming weeks.

articles.title_orig: China releases timeline for lunar landing on the Moon, targeting "before 2030"
articles.title_zh: China releases timeline for lunar landing on the Moon, targeting "before 2030"
articles.content_orig:
Chinese space officials confirmed this weekend that the Asian nation plans to land its astronauts on the Moon within three years.
At the Seventh Manned Spaceflight Conference in Beijing, officials, including Wang Xiang, chief designer for the lunar exploration program, laid out the country’s most publicly detailed plans yet for a series of missions leading up to a crewed lunar landing “before 2030.”
China’s lunar landings will involve a lunar-orbit rendezvous similar to what NASA did in the 1960s and early 1970s with the Apollo program. However, lacking a rocket as powerful as the Saturn V vehicle, the crew and lunar lander will launch separately to the Moon.
According to slides shared on social media, the current plan involves:
The public release of this new information provides a timeline for gauging China’s technical progress in its efforts to land humans on the Moon before 2030 and beat NASA and the United States back to the lunar surface.
Notably, the plan (for now, at least) omits a mission similar to Apollo 8 or Artemis II, which involved a crew flying out to the Moon and either entering orbit or passing close by before returning to Earth. The Mengzhou vehicle should still get a workout closer to Earth with humans on board as part of missions carrying astronauts to Tiangong, China’s space station in low-Earth orbit.
NASA has set a target of landing humans on the Moon by 2028, a year or so ahead of China. The United States, which has been working on the Space Launch System rocket for 15 years and the Orion spacecraft even longer, has a more established rocket and crew vehicle.
But there are major questions surrounding the development of a lunar lander, for which both SpaceX and Blue Origin have multibillion-dollar development contracts. Depending on how these projects go, a US lunar landing could be delayed to 2030 or even later.
Although it is virtually impossible for outsiders to glean information about technical milestones achieved inside China’s space program, the country is clearly making credible progress toward reaching the Moon. For example, in August 2025, the China Manned Space Agency successfully tested a high-fidelity mock-up of its 26-ton Lanyue lunar lander. The test used giant tethers to simulate lunar gravity as the vehicle fired its main engines and fine-control thrusters to land on a cratered surface and take off from a location near Beijing.
Recently, the Mengzhou spacecraft for the 2027 test atop a Long March 10A rocket arrived at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in Hainan, China, where the mission will launch.
US government assessments of the Chinese space program are restricted, but lawmakers are clearly taking the threat seriously. In the last 12 months, the US Congress and White House have given broad latitude to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman to streamline the Artemis Program to land humans on the Moon. He has moved swiftly to cancel the Lunar Gateway space station and planned upgrades to the Space Launch System rocket. And just last week, Isaacman announced plans to help Blue Origin develop a lunar lander by finding a way to boost the Orion spacecraft into low-lunar orbit.
“We have the mandate, we have the resources, and the support from our stakeholders to be able to execute, and that’s what we intend to do,” he said at the time.
For a couple of years, it has been clear that China has made a major commitment to landing astronauts on the Moon, preferably before the United States returns to the lunar surface, to score a major geopolitical win. Beyond this near-term competition, both NASA and China’s space program are building capabilities to establish a long-term presence at the Moon’s South Pole. As part of this second phase of the contest, Isaacman committed NASA to the development of a base on the surface of the Moon over the next decade.

articles.title_orig: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
articles.title_zh: Rivian Is Doing The Damn Thing
articles.content_orig:
There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.
Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .
Theoretically, things are only going to get better from here, sales-wise, with the only currently available R2 clocking in at $59,485, including destination. Eventually, a $55,485 Premium trim and $46,485 base model will join its ranks , but the only information we've got is "coming late 2026" and "coming spring 2027," respectively. Of course, even the most expensive R2 is a hell of a lot cheaper than the R1S and R1T, which both start well north of $80,000.
And good news keeps coming, because last week, Scaringe said he was "very confident" Rivian would hit an autonomy milestone this year that would unlock a quarter-billion-dollar tranche of investment money from Uber. That's part of an up-to $1.25 billion investment the rideshare company is making in the automaker through 2031, according to Reuters. It includes an initial $300 million and is contingent on several autonomy milestones. However, Rivian hasn't said exactly what those milestones are. Don't worry, though. Scaringe says Rivian is "right on time."
We do know that the partnership between Uber and Rivian targets the 2028 launch of a driverless R2 robotaxi on Uber's network — starting in a handful of cities and then expanding to about 25 over the next year and a half. Clearly, Rivian is aiming its R2 robotaxi directly at the Tesla Cybercab.
It needs to work, too. As Reuters points out, both the R2's success and the Uber partnership are imperative for making Rivian stick as a company. It's doing pretty well right now, don't get me wrong, but it's still burning through cash like the Bouvier Beale family, and it's looking for any way to narrow those losses.
No matter how you slice it, Rivian is truly showing it's a company that has the ability to stick around and be viable. Once R2 production is fully ramped up and the R3 is introduced, who knows where it could end up? All it needs to do is get that pesky cash burn problem under control.

articles.title_orig: Nearly Two Thousand Chinese Businesses Established in Nicaragua Since Free Trade Agreement Took Effect
articles.title_zh: Nearly Two Thousand Chinese Businesses Established in Nicaragua Since Free Trade Agreement Took Effect
articles.content_orig:
COSTA RICA'S LEADING ENGLISH LANGUAGE NEWSPAPER
Nearly 2,000 Chinese businesses have been established in Nicaragua during the first two years of the free trade agreement with China, according to the president of the Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua. Shujin Huang made the statement to official media outlets after an event marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen.
He said the association continues to promote additional investment from China, describing Nicaragua as a safe country with a competitive market. The free trade agreement between the two countries entered into force on January 1, 2024. The Banco Central de Nicaragua reported that net foreign direct investment from China reached 29.3 million dollars in 2025.
That figure represented 1.9 percent of the 1,502.5 million dollars in total net foreign direct investment recorded by the country that year. In 2024, any Chinese flows were not reported separately and would have been included in aggregate categories if present at all. Huang said the businesses operate mainly in commerce, with some also active in free-zone maquilas. The relatively low official investment total relative to the number of establishments indicates that most are small-scale operations.
The Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua was founded in May 2024 and was officially registered as a legal organization under Ministerial Agreement 24-2024-OSFL, allowing it to operate in its own name under Nicaraguan law. Its founding event included participation by Chinese Ambassador Chen Xi and Nicaraguan officials including National Assembly President Gustavo Porras, Foreign Minister Denis Moncada and Presidential Adviser Laureano Ortega Murillo.
As part of the commercial expansion, construction of a Chinatown complex advances in Managua near the Rotonda Universitaria. The project, also known as Plaza China or Plaza 101, involves a two-story structure of approximately 8,000 square meters with an investment of about 3 million dollars. It is planned to house around 100 businesses operated by Chinese, other Asian and Nicaraguan owners.
The site currently holds roughly 30 businesses. Administrators have described the work as being in an intermediate phase, including installation of a stone arch more than six meters high carved in a dragon style and brought from China. The complex is intended to concentrate commercial activity, gastronomy and cultural offerings. Huang cited the existing Plaza China as an example of growing Chinese capital presence, noting that more than ten foreign-investment businesses already operate there.
Nicaragua and China restored diplomatic relations in December 2021 after Managua broke ties with Taiwan. The free trade agreement was signed on August 31, 2023. Official Nicaraguan statements have presented the pact and related initiatives as measures to expand trade and investment opportunities. The association’s stated goals include supporting Chinese investors and promoting the policy of one China.
As of now, the association continues to encourage further arrivals of Chinese capital. Construction on the Managua Chinatown project remains under way, with officials and association representatives describing it as a visible marker of the commercial presence that has developed since the trade agreement took effect. The Banco Central de Nicaragua has not published a full country-by-country breakdown beyond the 2025 net total that places China at 29.3 million dollars.

articles.title_orig: Leicestershire Reform council leader quits after staff comments leaked
articles.title_zh: Leicestershire Reform council leader quits after staff comments leaked
articles.content_orig:
The Reform UK leader of Leicestershire County Council has announced he is standing down after comments he made about staff redundancies were leaked online.
Dan Harrison announced on Monday that he would be stepping down from the role he has held since May 2025.
He said he had made the decision after taking advice from senior Reform colleagues, and added deputy council leader Kevin Crook had taken over as acting leader.
It comes after Harrison had apologised after being recorded saying 76 council solicitors would be made redundant, branding them "incompetent", before saying "what I want to look at now is the women", in remarks which were then released on social media.
In a statement, Harrison said it had been the "honour of his life" to lead the county council's first Reform administration.
Harrison has said he will remain as a councillor, representing the Ashby-de-la-Zouch division.
The Conservative opposition at County Hall had called for Harrison to resign after his comments about staff were leaked.
In the recording, Harrison said: "There's 76 solicitors will be made redundant.
"We'll buy in the service, because [they are] incompetent. They're not doing a good job.
"What I want to look at now is the women so it is ongoing, I would like it to be at great pace but I can tell you now if we suddenly drove massive redundancies the liberals would walk away."
Earlier on Monday, Harrison had told the BBC he would not be stepping down - but he later said he made his decision after talking to Crook and group whip Andrew Hamilton-Gray.
He had apologised over the remarks, which were made on Tuesday during a Reform party meeting.
Despite his apology, Harrison had insisted his remarks had been taken out of context.
Harrison said: "I would like to apologise unreservedly to the staff and officers of the county council for any hurt, distress or offence caused by the publication of these comments, which were made during a heated meeting with the expectation of privacy and confidentiality.
"However, I would like to stress that these discussions were just that, and I have not given any instruction or direction to officers in these matters and that there has not been any discussion nor agreement on these issues with officers."
He added: "I unequivocally reject any suggestion that staffing decisions are being taken based on gender.
"The comments made in that meeting were taken completely out of context."
Before Harrison's resignation, the council's 15 Tory councillors had called for an emergency vote to try to remove him from the leader's role.
Group leader of the Conservative group, Deborah Taylor, said: "That was not a decision we took lightly.
"The serious concerns raised over recent days, particularly around the treatment of council employees and the comments contained in leaked recordings, left us feeling that his position had become untenable.
"His resignation brings an end to his leadership, but it does not mean those concerns should simply be forgotten.
"There are still questions that deserve answers, and it is important that the council learns from what has happened."
The Reform group remains the largest party on the authority, and runs it as a minority administration.
In a statement, Jeevun Sandher and Amanda Hack - Labour MPs for Loughborough and North West Leicestershire respectively - said: "Since taking office in 2025, the Reform UK administration has become increasingly embroiled in controversy and scandal, rather than focusing on delivering for the residents of Leicestershire.
"This is far from an isolated incident. Just last week, councillor [Joseph] Boam was found to have breached the council's own code of conduct through his actions against the former monitoring officer, while other Reform councillors have also been forced to apologise to residents over their behaviour. All of this in less than two years.
"Leicestershire residents deserve better."

articles.title_orig: Can Pakistan Help Break China’s Critical Minerals Dominance?
articles.title_zh: Can Pakistan Help Break China’s Critical Minerals Dominance?
articles.content_orig:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir before meeting with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office, on September 25, 2025. Pakistan’s  mineral wealth can help break China’s hold on the global critical minerals market, writes Derek Grossman. (The White House/Daniel Torok)
China has spent decades building a near-stranglehold on critical mineral supply chains, leaving the United States dangerously dependent on its chief strategic rival. Even President Donald Trump ’s recent trade truce with Chinese leader Xi Jinping has done little to resolve the underlying problem: America’s continued dependence on Chinese processing of minerals essential to its economy and national security. But the Trump administration is aggressively challenging Beijing’s dominance across the globe, and over the past year, it has engaged an unlikely partner: Pakistan .
To be sure, Pakistan has been an important, if at times complicated, American strategic partner since the Cold War, helping Washington counter Soviet expansionism and, after the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, supporting US military operations in Afghanistan . Bilateral ties have seen periods of strain, but Trump’s return to the White House has brought a major reboot. Since then, Trump has met multiple times with senior Pakistani leaders, including Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Most recently, Islamabad has served as a key mediator between the United States and Iran in efforts to end their war, ushering in a remarkable revival in bilateral relations.
And now, there’s apparently a new area to explore: critical minerals. Over the past year, the Trump administration has stepped up discussions with Islamabad on developing Pakistan’s largely untapped mineral wealth, including a $500 million agreement between an American company and Pakistan’s Frontier Works Organization to cooperate on mining and processing critical minerals, including rare earths.
Washington has also backed the massive Reko Diq copper and gold project through $1.25 billion in Export-Import Bank financing , underscoring its growing interest in Pakistan as an alternative source of strategic minerals. Pakistan, meanwhile, stands to benefit economically from greater American investment in a mining sector that currently accounts for only about 3 percent of its GDP.
Last April, a US delegation led by Eric Meyer of the State Department attended the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad and conveyed the interest of American companies in the sector. With the forum returning November 12–13 , renewed American participation—particularly if accompanied by fresh investment commitments—would demonstrate that Washington is serious about turning its growing interest in Pakistan’s mineral wealth into a lasting strategic partnership.
Deeper US-Pakistan cooperation on critical minerals could help Washington chip away at Beijing’s dominance over global supply chains. Early American investment could also help determine where Pakistan’s minerals are processed and who ultimately purchases them, rather than allowing Beijing to lock in these arrangements before Washington has a chance to compete.
Indeed, Pakistan is just one piece of the Trump administration’s broader strategy to reduce dependence on China, with Washington pursuing critical minerals agreements and partnerships across Asia, including Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Australia, as well as resource-rich countries such as Argentina, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Ukraine.
Washington’s experience in Africa suggests the bet can pay off. The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a country where conflict in the east has complicated the operating environment and where Chinese firms have long held the advantage, yet the United States has leaned in anyway, building on a Lobito Corridor initiative that began under the Biden administration and that Trump has carried forward. In December 2025, Washington and Kinshasa signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement reportedly giving American companies a right of first offer on designated mineral deposits.
This July, the Development Finance Corporation and the Development Bank of Southern Africa closed a $753 million package to upgrade the Lobito Atlantic Railway, which carries Congolese and Zambian copper and cobalt to Angola’s Atlantic coast, and the operator now expects to double its international cargo to 800,000 tons next year .
In May, the DRC’s state cobalt entity also agreed to supply cobalt hydroxide to a US-based firm. Progress has not been linear, and the DRC’s task force for the minerals pact was set up months behind schedule, but the lesson is clear: sustained commitment in a difficult jurisdiction can reshape supply chains in ways that waiting for ideal conditions never will. Pakistan has its own challenges, but trust built through early investment is what gives American companies a seat at the table.
But challenges remain. For starters, Pakistan’s evolving domestic security situation, particularly in mineral-rich Balochistan, will shape how quickly American companies can establish an on-the-ground presence. The Barrick Mining Corporation has slowed development of the massive Reko Diq copper and gold project while it reviews the security environment in Pakistan and the wider region, though it has said it continues to believe in the project’s long-term value and has kept Phase 1 approved, a reminder that investors will need to price in risk and that Islamabad has a strong interest in improving the conditions for them.
Another constraint is that Beijing, having entered Pakistan’s mining sector much earlier, already enjoys significant advantages in infrastructure, expertise, and established commercial relationships, forcing Washington to play catch-up. According to a recent Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) report, China already purchases approximately 95 percent of Pakistan’s exported copper ores and concentrates, illustrating just how deeply Beijing is embedded in Pakistan’s existing minerals trade.
Nevertheless, the upcoming critical minerals conference, along with potential new Trump administration agreements with Islamabad, could help narrow this gap—provided they translate into concrete investments and sustained cooperation. Moreover, much of Pakistan’s critical mineral wealth remains underexplored, giving American companies a chance to help identify and develop commercially viable deposits, particularly antimony—a strategically important critical mineral used in ammunition, explosives, flame retardants, and advanced military technologies, making it essential to US defense manufacturing and national security—while potentially establishing new processing facilities outside China’s control. Islamabad also has an incentive to welcome American investment as a way to diversify its economic relationships without abandoning its longstanding strategic partnership with Beijing.
Though making that case a reality will take more than just this. Washington could start by pairing its financing with tools that help American firms manage the risks of a frontier jurisdiction, such as political risk insurance and co-financing alongside development banks and Gulf investors, so that capital can move before conditions are perfect. It should prioritize processing as much as extraction, because the real leverage lies in refining, and the opportunity to build facilities outside China’s control is greatest while Pakistan’s sector is still taking shape.
And it should treat the relationship as a durable economic partnership rather than an extension of its diplomacy around Iran, with offtake agreements and technical cooperation that give both sides a stake in the outcome. articles.title_orig: SpaceX weighs Boost Mobile deal in push for Starlink phone service: Report
articles.title_zh: SpaceX weighs Boost Mobile deal in push for Starlink phone service: Report
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
SpaceX ( SPCX ) may be attempting an end run to circumvent obstacles it's facing in getting a mobile network off the ground.
Per the Washington Post , SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar ( SATS ) about launching its own wireless phone service through Boost Mobile, after the country's three biggest carriers — Verizon, AT&T ( T ), and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) — reportedly turned down SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Musk met with EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen last month, according to two people familiar with the negotiations cited by the Post. The talks could end with SpaceX buying Boost Mobile outright or getting access to its network, which the discount carrier leases from AT&T and T-Mobile.
In recent months, Musk asked the heads of Verizon ( VZ ), AT&T and T-Mobile to let SpaceX use their networks for its own mobile service. All three said no, per the Post.
But there may be a catch to SpaceX's plan. Typically, a carrier's lease agreement can't be transferred to a new owner without the host carrier's permission, meaning AT&T and T-Mobile may still need to approve a Boost deal to provide access to SpaceX.
SpaceX is open about its ambitions in the terrestrial mobile space. On the company's recent earnings call , CFO Bret Johnsen said the goal is to "become a major mobile carrier ... in the United States." SpaceX also recently agreed to buy $8 billion worth of wireless spectrum licenses intended for cellular service in places satellites can't reach.
"This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," Musk said on X .
SpaceX and EchoStar already have a relationship. In September 2025, SpaceX agreed to buy EchoStar's AWS-4 and H-block spectrum licenses for about $17 billion, split between up to $8.5 billion in cash and up to $8.5 billion in SpaceX stock, EchoStar said at the time . SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said the deal would "advance our mission to end mobile dead zones."
What SpaceX still lacks is a ground network. Its satellite signal isn't strong enough yet to carry cell coverage indoors or in dense cities, where most phones are - and that's why a deal with Boost would be so crucial.
An MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) like Boost rents capacity on an existing carrier's network. Last month, TD Cowen's Gregory Williams called acquiring an MVNO the cheapest and fastest route for SpaceX to launch mobile service, noting a network build would cost "upwards of $80B" and take years.
The Big 3, he said, still show no desire "to (ever) sign an MVNO deal with Starlink that could ravage the industry."
Carrier executives have publicly doubted that SpaceX can rebuild their tower networks. Verizon's CEO put the build-out at four to six years. Musk said it would take about half that.
"Veterans of the cellular industry look at the chess board of existing pieces and don't see a solution," Musk said recently on X . "They don't understand that SpaceX is developing entirely new pieces that fundamentally alter the strategic landscape."

articles.title_orig: China’s AI Data Centers Move West, But Their Tax Revenue Stays East - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: China’s AI Data Centers Move West, But Their Tax Revenue Stays East - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
When Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia in mid-October, he was briefed on its computing industry and called for efforts to “extend the industrial chain” and keep “transforming the strength in computing into development advantages.” Ulanqab is cold, electricity is cheap, and Beijing is close , so the city became a hub of the data-center boom powering China’s AI race with the United States. Yet a city official told the Economic Observer that the industry is still “losing money” and that tax revenue will build up gradually only once projects under construction start operating.
After the data centers open, however, the companies selling cloud services and AI models pay the tax on those sales in Hangzhou and Beijing, where they are registered. Most of the tax that stays in Ulanqab is paid during construction. If nothing changes, Ulanqab will struggle to turn its computing advantage into a development advantage of its own.
In China, where tax is paid depends on where the invoicing company is registered. Both value-added tax (VAT) and corporate income tax are paid there , and the local government keeps half of the VAT and 40 percent of the corporate income tax . If you rent a server on Alibaba Cloud, you can choose a data center in Ulanqab, but the invoice comes from the company registered in Hangzhou.
Alibaba and ByteDance both have subsidiaries in Ulanqab, but those subsidiaries do not invoice customers for cloud services and AI models. Alibaba Cloud lists the companies that invoice for its main products . None of them is a wholly owned Alibaba subsidiary in Ulanqab, and none is registered in Inner Mongolia. ByteDance registered three subsidiaries in the city in 2026, yet invoices for its cloud business, Volcano Engine , still come from a Beijing company.
In the same Economic Observer report, a local tax official said a data center generates most of its local tax during construction. Once a data center is operating, company headquarters sell most of its data services. What remains locally is mainly taxes on land and buildings and employees’ personal income tax. The number of employees is limited, however; a completed gigawatt-scale campus usually has only a few hundred operations staff .
Not much revenue stays where the data center is built. In 2025, Ulanqab’s computing industry paid 368 million yuan ($55 million) in tax , less than 5 percent of the city’s revenue. China Taxation News , the State Taxation Administration’s newspaper, reported that tax from the city’s computing industry rose more than 60 percent year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026. But construction has not stopped, so that increase cannot tell us what happens after the data centers open. When construction ends, construction-phase tax will recede. Taxes on land and buildings recur every year, but they depend on the site and the property, not on sales.
Liu Huansuo, deputy director of Ulanqab’s big data administration, told Xinhua : “If we rely solely on cheap electricity and low land costs, we risk becoming little more than ‘landlords of server rooms.’” That is a problem for Ulanqab’s finances.
In 2025, the city’s own revenue covered less than a fifth of its spending, and higher levels of government supplied more than half of its available funds. Those governments decide how much Ulanqab receives; the city decides for itself how to spend local tax revenue. Yet as data centers based in Ulanqab sell more and more cloud and AI services, the tax revenue goes to Hangzhou and Beijing. If Ulanqab is to “extend the industrial chain,” it will probably still need money from higher levels of government.
Some places in China do capture the tax on cloud services because the invoicing company is registered locally. Gui’an New Area in Guizhou is one of them. In the first 10 months of 2025, digital companies in Gui’an recorded 75.2 billion yuan ($11.2 billion) in invoiced sales , nearly 90 percent of it from 18 firms, including Huawei Cloud and Tencent. Huawei Cloud has announced that contracts and invoices for its customers in China will mainly be signed and issued by a company registered in Gui’an. Firms are willing to register an invoicing company in Gui’an, but they will not set one up everywhere they have a data center.
Alibaba and ByteDance can argue the profit comes from their models and customers, so paying the tax at headquarters is reasonable. That is a fair point, yet it leaves the host area in the lurch. Ulanqab can keep the tax paid during construction and the taxes on land and buildings, but neither will grow the way sales do to support sustainable development.
As the national “East Data, West Computing” program moves data centers west to power China’s AI push, other western places that host data centers face the same arithmetic – unless the invoicing companies register there. Ulanqab’s 109 signed data-center projects are expected to come online within two to three years. Once construction stops, the city’s tax take from computing may stop growing, and with it the chance to turn data centers into lasting development.

articles.title_orig: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.title_zh: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.content_orig:
After many months of discussion , Apple has figured out a way to bring Apple Intelligence to China, working with Alibaba’s Qwen model on some features. Apple Intelligence will soon be made available as a developer beta and will ship to Chinese customers in December with iOS 27.3.
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved the use of Alibaba AI models with the iPhone in October 2026. Confirming the complexity of bringing these tools to China, Apple also received clearance in July from the Cyberspace Administration of China. Apple watchers are at liberty to reflect that the news comes at the best possible time for the company, which continues to grow smartphone market share in China.
The promise of integrated AI support in the form of Apple Intelligence can only boost interest in the company’s recently introduced iPhone Duo . Recent Counterpoint Research data claims iPhone sales increased 29% year on year in China in the three weeks following launch of the 18 Pro series devices. Initial stock of the devices sold out in hours.
China is also the world’s biggest market for foldable devices, which prompted some enterprising individuals to attempt to resell purchased iPhone Duos for far above their store price — scalpers have since reduced prices , because even in iPhone-crazy China, people weren’t willing to pay so much.
While it’s a big step for Apple AI in China, it’s not quite the great leap Apple may have wanted to put in place.
Siri AI is not supported and won’t be “anytime soon,” according to market speculation . While little is said about the reasons for that, it seems probable that political pressure in both the US and China may be partly to blame, as both nations see control of the means of AI production as essential for the future success of their differing ideologies. Apple has had to allow the Chinese government to approve ongoing updates to the suite.
Chinese users can use Alibaba’s Qwen in Siri, writing tools, and visual intelligence, including functions related to text and image understanding. They don’t get Image Playground, but can expect:
Apple and Alibaba also promise to maintain privacy. Customers will be able to choose if they wish to proceed with making a request through Qwen. Alibaba also said it would not use these requests for model training, though it isn’t yet clear if requests are going to Private Cloud Compute in Apple’s Chinese AI deployment.
Will the introduction of Apple Intelligence in China make a difference? It probably already is, as months of ever stronger speculation mean most Chinese consumers knew Apple AI was coming to their iPhones even as they purchased them before the announcement took place.
While the initial sales rush on Apple’s new devices among Chinese consumers has slowed, the news may help generate fresh enthusiasm for the iPhone in China. That’s great for Apple, but not such great news for some smaller smartphone vendors, who continue to be hammered by vicious increases in memory and other component prices.
Speaking almost two years ago when industry observers had anticipated an Apple Intelligence launch in China would take place earlier, Morgan Stanley then suggested the Alibaba partnership would be “a critical catalyst for Apple’s competitive standing in China.”
Other than painful price increases, not much has changed, and the introduction can only help consolidate the iPhone’s appeal in China. That’s good for Apple’s customers there, and great news for Apple’s investors everywhere else. It may even do something to retain a little US soft power.
In the background, we see the continued economic pressure wrought by fast-increasing memory prices. This has driven smartphone makers to raise prices, which has itself driven a 21% year on year decline in sector sales .
Apple and Samsung have proved more resilient to these price hikes than others, which means the added appeal generated by the launch of Apple Intelligence in the world’s second-largest economy is likely to make a highly significant difference to its market share in the short term, as well as shoring up share in future replacement cycles.
Now please subscribe to my daily, human-curated Apple-related news headline feed at The Core , or follow me on BlueSky , LinkedIn , or Mastodon .
Hello, and thanks for dropping in. I'm pleased to meet you. I'm Jonny Evans, and I've been writing (mainly about Apple) since 1999. These days I write my daily AppleHolic blog at Computerworld.com, where I explore Apple's growing identity in the enterprise. You can also keep up with my work at AppleMust , and follow me on BlueSky , Mastodon , and LinkedIn .

articles.title_orig: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.title_zh: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.content_orig:
China is stepping up its diplomatic efforts in the Middle East, including over the US-Israel war on Iran , following a lapse in activity.
Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Monday met a senior Iranian security official in Beijing, while President Xi Jinping hosted Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq for a landmark state visit.
Wang told Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, that dialogue and negotiation remained “the only viable path forward” as conflicts in the region “drag on and risk further spillover”.
He also reaffirmed China’s support for Iran’s sovereignty and security. Beijing has consistently blamed the US and Israel for starting the conflict.
“China is very close to Tehran; it is the biggest trading partner of Iran, the biggest customer of Iranian crude,” said Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing.
However, Beijing’s diplomacy efforts have recently been stalled, she noted.
“It’s been a few weeks or even months [in which] China really hasn’t done much diplomatically towards … ending the war,” Yu said.
The meetings on Monday appear to illustrate that China is growing impatient with the lack of progress.
“I think China is very frustrated, and it wants to be seen to enter [the process],” Yu said.
Reflecting the step up in activity, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Monday that Zhai Jun, Beijing’s special envoy on the Middle East, will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.
Meanwhile, Xi received Sultan Haitham, the first Omani head of state to visit China since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 1978.
The Chinese president said the Middle East and Gulf “should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict”.
Sitting across from Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, Oman is a key player in navigation on the strategic waterway, through which one-fifth of global energy exports traversed before the US-Iran war restricted traffic.
China is one of the world’s largest energy importers. Xi described bilateral ties with Oman as being at a “new historical starting point”.
During the visit, China and Oman signed 14 cooperation documents, covering areas including artificial intelligence, green energy and supply chains, along with a currency swap agreement.
In a joint statement, they called for safe navigation to resume through Hormuz and urged the US and Iran to restart dialogue.
Yu said the conflict had made the relationship “more of a priority for both sides”, particularly given the disruption to China’s energy imports.
“Oman is particularly important because many of its ports are outside the strait,” she said.

articles.title_zh: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe, Belgium launches investigation
articles.content_orig:
Dozens of supermarkets in Europe have reported temperatures of their refrigerators and fridges rising overnight, now widely believed to be caused by cyber attacks similar to the one that affected France several weeks ago.
Supermarket chains in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia, Netherlands, Luxembourg and Ireland have been affected.
The story began with Belgian media reporting on Monday that fridges were turned up to 17 degrees Celsius, forcing many stores to throw away food.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity (CCB) told Belgian outlet Belga that it is aware of an incident targeting supermarket refrigeration systems.
CCB spokesperson Katrien Eggers told Euronews Next, "We are aware of an incident, but have no further information." There are no reports yet as to who was behind the attack... and it may never be possible to identify them."
Belgium's federal prosecutor's office have opened an investigation into the incident, according to a spokesperson.
Some 40 Delhaize Proxy supermarkets, 15 Carrefour Shop & Go stores, 15 Intermarché shops and five Spar Q8 service station locations have reportedly been impacted in Belgium, according to Belgian outlet Le Soir .
Butchery group De Laet en Van Haver also said that their fridges were affected. IKEA have also said their Bergen shop located at Mons was affected, bringing the total to 75 stores affected in Belgium.
"We have identified an IT incident affecting the refrigeration systems in several dozen stores. We immediately took the necessary measures to keep our stores operational," a spokesperson from Delhaize told Euronews Next.
Carrefour told Euronews Next this morning that "the impact at Carrefour is very limited: currently 15 of our 700 stores are affected, both in Flanders and Wallonia. Not a single hypermarket is among them."
"All stores remain open because it only concerns a few refrigeration units, mainly freezers. Quick action was taken so that all stores can stay open," they added.
Meanwhile later this morning Carrefour Belgium spokesman Mich Vergauwen said, "It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," adding that the "impact is very limited".
It's believed the incident took place between Sunday night and Monday morning, skyrocketing refrigerator temperatures.
Stephan Moelans, CEO of refrigeration installer Sabcobel, which manages Delhaize's fridges and freeze systems, told the Belga news outlet that the Belgian attack involves exactly the same mechanism as the previous French cyberattack.
"Over the past few weeks, we've been working very hard to protect our customers' fridges against this vulnerability," Moelans said.
He said the incident happened when the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
The refrigeration executive said a software update alone is not enough to address the vulnerability, with physical modifications required instead.
"That requires investment. The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France."
Sabcobel know of around twenty affected units, out of the hundreds it manages across Belgium.
Danfoss, the company that supplied the software for the refrigeration systems affected in both the latest incident and the one in France in October, said customers who had not updated their software were affected.
A spokesperson told VTM NIEUWS that "the company says that the vulnerability lies primarily in outdated software and that they had already urged customers to start using their new software".
Problems reportedly also occurred at a number of stores of the Swedish supermarket chains ICA and Coop last night, with refrigerators and freezers turned up to 50 degrees Celsius.
A similar incident occurred in Estonian at one location of supermarket chain Selver, according to media reports.
13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were affected by a suspected cyber incident, according to a statement by owner Musgrave made to the Irish Times.
In the Netherlands, the freezing and cooling systems of at least seventeen companies were attacked last night, according to a spokesperson for supplier Danfoss. The identities of the companies were not disclosed.
Delhaize also suspended its ordering systems in Luxembourg as a precaution to prevent a similar incident.
Finnish media report that several K Group supermarkets have been affected. K Group is one of Finland's largest retail chains.
These reported incidents follow a similar attack in France just weeks ago, on 12 October, when hundreds of French supermarkets belonging to the Intermarché and Coopérative U chains fell victim to a cyberattack targeting their refrigeration systems.

articles.title_orig: European supermarkets targeted in reported cyberattacks stretching from Ireland to Sweden
articles.title_zh: European supermarkets targeted in reported cyberattacks stretching from Ireland to Sweden
articles.content_orig:
Temperature settings were increased, resulting in food spoilage, companies said.
Grocery stores in several European countries are dealing with incidents affecting refrigerator and freezer systems that appear to be the results of cyberattacks.
Refrigeration systems have been malfunctioning Monday in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, The Netherlands and Estonia, officials from affected companies told ABC News and local public broadcasters.
In each of the incidents, the reported cyberattacks altered the settings and functioning of refrigerator and freezer units, resulting in food spoilage.
The targets appear to have been smaller stores and have affected only a limited number of each chain's retail locations, according to statements obtained by ABC News.
Swedish grocery store chains ICA and Coop confirmed to ABC News that some of its stores had been affected, with ICA saying there was an "incident overnight affecting a small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA’s central network," and Coop saying the incident affected "seven out of more than 800 stores."
The situation was "contained and under control," according to a Coop spokesperson.
Coop added that the incident occurred ahead of a planned system upgrade, which had been in the works because of a similar issue affecting French grocery stores last month, in which hundreds of stores saw the fridges and freezers similarly hacked and temperatures set to 50 degrees Celsius, or 122 degrees Fahrenheit. Most of the systems targeted then were reportedly using outdated software.
One ICA grocery store in Sjöbo, Sweden, posted to social media that "overnight, our refrigerators and freezers were hacked, and the temperature was set to 50 degrees."
Belgian supermarket chains Delhaize and Carrefour were also affected, representatives for the companies told ABC News, with Delhaize referring to it as an "IT incident."
"[T]he impact at Carrefour is very limited: currently 15 of our 700 stores are affected," a spokesperson told ABC News, adding "all stores remain open because it only concerns a few refrigeration units, mainly freezers."
Musgrave, the company that owns Irish grocery chain SuperValu, told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that 13 stores had been affected by a suspected cyberattack that affected a specific refrigeration model.
Dutch refrigeration company Danfoss told public broadcaster NOS that seventeen facilities using its refrigeration systems, such as frozen product storage and butcher shops, were affected by a cyberattack of the kind that hit French stores last month. Danfoss systems were affected at the time in France as well.
Several military bases in the U.S. experienced similar cyberattacks in August, according to Reuters , which said at least six commissaries -- on-base grocery stores -- had been affected in ways similar to the recent European attacks, including the October incidents in France. The Pentagon is investigating the incidents, according to Reuters.

articles.title_orig: Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content
articles.title_zh: Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content
articles.content_orig:
One of the classics that helped create an entire genre, stealth masterpiece Thief: The Dark Project is coming to PS5 in remastered form next month, from 3rd December 2026.
This new version of the 1998 game has been remastered using Nightdive Studios' KEX Engine to produce a new edition running at 4K and 120 frames-per-second. It's got all the content of the base game, the three extra missions from Thief: Gold, and an entirely new campaign in the form of The Tarnished Mirror.
The Tarnished Mirror is a narrative bridge between The Dark Project and Thief 2: The Metal Age . In it, "a seemingly straightforward theft spirals into imprisonment, uneasy alliances and a descent into a drowned, R’lyeh-like necropolis. Players will experience an expanded enemy roster, ambitious level design and a pure Thief experience that descends into unsettling, otherworldly horror."
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
The bonus campaign has been created by the same people who made Thief: The Black Parade , which was a mod / expansion for Thief: Gold, made by the fans. "This collaboration marks a rare industry moment, with Nightdive and Eidos-Montréal welcoming a community creation directly into official canon," the press release added.
You can also expect the following from the remastered package:
Pre-orders are live on the PS Store for the PS5 digital versions, with a standard edition costing £24.99 / $29.99 and a Digital Deluxe Edition priced at £28.99 / $34.99.
In terms of physical editions, you're looking at three versions to choose from: standard, steelbook, and deluxe trapezoid. The first two are self-explanatory, but the Deluxe Trapezoid edition includes the game, steelbook, booklet, a box, and a physical remaster diary for £49.99 / $69.99:
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
This looks amazing. Big fan of Thief Gold so this package looks like the best it’s ever been.

I'm seeing less and less context/text in art-books now. That steelbook is nice too. I'm not sure what sleeves included means, but to see them credit the illustrator too is such a good move, Clear River Games clearly know what they are doing.

articles.title_orig: Honda Africa Twin range gets bigger engine, fresh technology, and brand-new model lines
articles.title_zh: Honda Africa Twin range gets bigger engine, fresh technology, and brand-new model lines
articles.content_orig:
Honda have announced major changes to their Africa Twin adventure bike family for 2027, confirming new models, plus a capacity jump from 1084cc to 1131cc across the line-up.
Now known as the CRF1150L, the range will consist of a standard base model, plus the road-focussed Adventure Sports (AS) as before. A new off-road centric Enduro Sports will also join the brigade, with a raised front mudguard and spoked 21in front wheel.
Starting with the Adventure Sports, the base version will be joined by a new top of the line CRF1150L Africa Twin Adventure Sports Honda Sensing Ride – fitted with front and rear radar to compete against the likes of the new Triumph Tiger 1200 , and fully-specced BMW R1300GS .
Exclusively available with Honda’s semi-automatic Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) system, the Sensing Ride is joined by two standard CRF1150L AS variants – one with a conventional manual gearbox and another with DCT in place.
All three are expected in UK dealers from March and put out a claimed 117.3bhp at 7500rpm and 87.8lb.ft of torque at 5750rpm, with the updated parallel-twin motor housed in a revised steel frame which – combined with an aluminium swingarm – cuts a claimed 1.4kg over the outgoing structure.
That’s not to say the bikes are lightweights though – far from it – with kerb weights starting at 245kg for the conventional manual, raising to 255kg for the AS with DCT. The Sensing Ride version tips the scales at 256kg – with all three getting 220mm of ground clearance and an adjustable seat height of between 830-850mm.
All three are fed by a 24.2-litre fuel tank, with Honda promising 55.4mpg for the manual version and 52.3mpg for the semi-automatic flavours. This fuel tank runs under the seat, which Honda says helps contribute to a greater mass centralisation of weight – helping the bikes to feel less top heavy and potentially more composed on the go.
This is combined with a re-positioned battery, ECU, fuel filler cap, and airbox – with Honda also keen to make life easier when manoeuvring at low speeds, especially handy when loaded up with luggage and/or a pillion passenger .
Being the road-biased version, all three roll on a 19in front and 18in rear spoked wheel, shod with a choice of Bridgestone Battlax Adventure A41s, or Michelin Anakee Roads.
Not only this, but the riding position has also been tweaked, with the handlebars now 10mm narrower and 10mm higher and further forward. The footpegs are also 10mm further forward and 20mm narrower, too.
Away from the numbers, the Africa Twins are now even cleverer than before, with Honda promising six standard riding modes that can all be personalised to the rider’s preferences. There’s also an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) for lean-sensitive rider modes, and backlit switchgear that’s said to be less complex than the current design.
The Sensing Ride takes this further with front and rear radar guidance – a first for the Africa Twin – unlocking rider support including blind spot detection, adaptive cruise control, and group ride assistance.
Alongside this, you’ll also find front and rearward collision warnings, plus ‘Distance Assist’ (to stop you getting too close to the vehicle in front on a manual throttle), and an ‘Emergency Brake Assist’ that applies some stopping power when there is a collision risk up front.
Being the clutchless DCT variant, it also gets ‘Stop & Go’, which lets the bike follow the vehicle in front during stop start traffic – a similar set-up to the semi-automatic KTM 1390 Super Adventure S Evo , launched for the beginning of 2026.
It doesn’t end there either because the Adventure Sports trio come on Showa electronic suspension as standard, known as Electronically Equipped Ride Adjustment (or EERA for short).
Working through a monoshock and chunky 49mm upside down front forks (up from 45mm), it is combined with Honda Skyhook control that continuously monitors the position of the bike to adjust damping forces in a bid improve handling, stability, and ride quality.
The EERA system itself takes data from sources including the ECU, IMU and fork stroke sensor to adjust damping by the millisecond – with 210mm of travel available at the front end, and 200mm available at the rear.
As is the way with many modern adventure bikes, a ‘Minimum’ mode will also lower the seat height by 5mm for a flatter foot and remains selected even after you’ve switched off the bike.
There’s also a raft of preload settings too, consisting of ‘Solo’, ‘Solo with Luggage’, ‘Pillion’, and ‘Pillion with Full Luggage’. Adjustment can then be further fine-tuned, including 24-steps of preload – with further electronic interventions including hill hold control, and electronically combined ABS that monitors brake pressure in the calipers at both ends for smoother applications.
Alongside the Adventure Sports comes a new CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports model, which shares many of the same creature comforts, but comes based around the updated standard model.
Promising a 9kg weight reduction, it’s distinguish it from its siblings by a pointed front beak, and HRC-style paint – however performance still comes from the same new 1131cc parallel-twin engine, meaning an identical 117.3bhp at 7500rpm and 87.8lb.ft of torque at 5750rpm.
Just like the standard model, it rolls on a 21in front and 18in spoked rim with tubeless Metzeler Karoo Street tyres, and shares the same steel frame, aluminium swingarm, riding position, electronics, and updated seven inch TFT display (with additional 5.7in screen) – with a choice of manual or DCT gearboxes available to order.
Keyless ignition, cruise control, and handguards come as standard – as do six customisable riding modes, plus an adjustable seat height of between 870mm and 890mm plus a kerb weight of 228kg for the manual and 239kg for the DCT.
Like the Adventure Sports, you’ll find CarPlay and Android Auto, with the bike receiving a higher 260mm of ground clearance and fully-adjustable 49mm closed-cartridge forks inspired by the brand’s CRF450 Rally competition bike.
Suspension comes via Showa at both ends, with 240mm of travel up front and 230mm at the rear. This works with sizeable 310mm floating wavey front discs, plus an advanced array of lean-sensitive electronics including seven stage Honda Selectable Torque Control (or traction control) which meters the amount of intervention on the throttle on- or off-road, depending on inputs from the six-axis IMU.
Other features include wheelie control, and traction can be switched off altogether if required. Unlike the Adventure Sports, the fuel capacity drops to 18.8 litres, thanks to an altered dual-tank design – however the same overall adventure bike silhouette remains.
Although still sitting at the lower end of the big adventure bike power figures, Honda’s Africa Twin motor has undergone some significant development for 2027.
For starters, there’s a redesigned intake system, plus larger-diameter 52mm throttle bodies (up from 46mm), and a revised valvetrain and cylinder head – with Honda promising an increased compression ratio from 10.5:1 to now 12.1:1.
The pistons have also changed, as have the con rods, crankshaft and balancer shafts – with options for both a six-speed manual or semi-automatic Dual Clutch Transmission system (that both share the same crankcase design).
Honda have brought the Africa Twin right up-to-date with these changes, however the fresh engine is still lacking the performance figures of some its premium big-capacity rivals. Whether you need all that punch is debatable, but the fresh electronics and revised riding position should make it a strong contender whether you fancy a trip across Europe by road, or by trail.
News Editor, trackday fan, lover of 90s sportsbikes

articles.title_orig: Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europe
articles.title_zh: Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europe
articles.content_orig:
Suspected cyberattacks have triggered temperatures to rise in grocery store refrigeration systems in a growing number of countries across Europe.
Overnight temperature spikes were recorded in stores in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden. On Monday, retailers and authorities pointed to alleged cyberattacks that underscored the vulnerability of systems that once largely operated mechanically.
The head of ⁠⁠⁠⁠Sweden’s national cybersecurity centre, John Billow, confirmed on Monday to the Reuters news agency that the centre ⁠⁠⁠⁠is responding to ⁠⁠⁠⁠multiple incidents affecting store cooling systems.
“We have in recent weeks … identified that we have quite a lot of exposed operational technology devices in Sweden that we have been clear about the necessity to update or patch,” he said.
The temperature of freezers in several Swedish stores rose suddenly overnight, store operators ICA and Coop said, while Swedish retailer Axfood said freezers at a distribution centre for home delivery of groceries in the Gothenburg area were hacked.
SuperValu, Ireland’s third-largest supermarket chain, ⁠⁠⁠⁠said a specific model of refrigeration systems has been affected by a “cyber incident” at 13 of its 223 ⁠⁠⁠⁠stores.
The Belga news agency reported overnight temperature increases at dozens of ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Ahold Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg. They were blamed on a cyberattack, according to the chief ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠executive ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠of refrigeration company,⁠ ⁠⁠⁠Sabcobel.
Stephan Moelans said the units’ evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
Also in Belgium, five Spar shops had their fridge systems attacked, said a spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates the franchise system.
In Estonia, at least one supermarket chain was affected, technology supplier Kitman Coldtech told public broadcaster ERR.
“This is very fresh, it happened this morning,” Kitman’s CEO Jann Mutso said, without naming the affected chain.
Ahold Delhaize reported a cybersecurity incident to Dutch police last month.
The cyberattack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets in France raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F), spoiling food and causing fires at several stores.
One Swedish store said in a social media post on Monday that the temperature of its refrigerators and freezers had been set to the same temperature as during the cyberattack in France.
“We are aware that a limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems,” a spokesperson for privately held ICA told Reuters in an email.
Kitman’s Mutso also said that temperatures at the Estonian chain were set to 50 degrees Celsius (122F).
Privately-held retailer Coop told Swedish daily Aftonbladet that six of its stores had been affected by similar incidents.
There has been no claim of responsibility for Monday’s attack, nor the one earlier in France.
However, the incidents help to increase concern regarding hybrid warfare stemming from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the Iran-United States war.
European states have blamed Moscow for a growing number of incidents affecting infrastructure, including via cyberattacks, in recent months. Russia has repeatedly denied involvement in any sabotage or hybrid warfare operations.
European Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Christophe Hansen said the attacks were “a deliberate attempt ⁠to disrupt” EU food supplies and undermine public ‌confidence.
“These incidents show that cyberattacks ⁠can disrupt services, affect ⁠businesses and directly affect citizens’ ⁠daily lives”, a ⁠European Commission spokesperson ⁠said, stressing the importance of strengthening ‌cybersecurity across the bloc.
A spokesperson for The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium told Al Jazeera that the rising number of cyberattack incidents, especially those resulting from the targeted use of AI, is an evolving trend.
However, they added, “we may never be able to identify … who is behind this attack”.

articles.title_orig: Goodbye to the toilet brush: the more hygienic alternative more and more bathrooms are switching to
articles.title_zh: Goodbye to the toilet brush: the more hygienic alternative more and more bathrooms are switching to
articles.content_orig:
TheCoolist is a mood board for your headspace.
It sits next to every toilet, usually in a closed holder, and a Finnish cleaning expert says many people keep it far too long. In Scandinavia and Central Europe, home sites report that many households are now swapping the classic bristle toilet brush for a different design. Here’s what is replacing it, why cleaning pros say it’s more hygienic, and what it still can’t do.
According to the Norwegian site Dagens.no , many people are choosing a silicone brush over the traditional plastic one. The reasons it gives: there are no dense bristles for dirt to collect in, so the head rinses clean; the flexible head reaches the edges and hard-to-access areas; it tends to spray less; and it is often sold with a ventilated or wall-mounted holder that lets it dry faster. The site quotes Finnish cleaning expert Mari Breilin, who says plastic brushes should be replaced considerably more often than many people do. The price, it adds, is about the same as many ordinary brushes.
The British testing site Expert Reviews sums it up: bristles are “so tightly packed together that it’s impossible to clean them perfectly,” so “bacteria build-up on the brush is inevitable,” and they “need replacing much more often.” Cleaning expert Isabella Flores, of Sparkly Maid San Diego, told Tom’s Guide that silicone is non-porous, so it doesn’t absorb bacteria and organic matter the way plastic bristles can. It also dries faster and tolerates harsher disinfection, including boiling.
Silicone or not, the routine is what keeps it hygienic. Tom’s Guide recommends:
Silicone is not a miracle. Expert Reviews notes that silicone brushes shaped like regular ones “usually have weak bristles that don’t do a great job on stubborn dirt,” and that flat, spatula-style heads handle grime better, though you have to get used to a different technique. And no brush, silicone or bristle, is built to dissolve the hard mineral ring at the waterline. And whatever you choose, a brush kept damp in a closed holder will still breed bacteria.
For that waterline ring, here’s the best way to remove limescale from the toilet . The bathroom is changing in other ways too, like the option replacing toilet paper , and the floor around the base deserves attention: see why people are spraying vinegar around the toilet .
A flat silicone head, an open holder and a date to replace it. That’s the trick.
